BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r1.claim: The Persian verse says tribulation brings nearness and friendship with God, while patience, piety, and obedience to the Lord rank highest for mystics.
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r1.anchor: صبر وتقوى وطاعت مولى نزد عارف زهر شرف اولى

BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r2.claim: The initial إنّا uses a majestic plural nūn according to scholars; knowers instead see the nūn as indicating the plurality of divine names and attributes.
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r2.anchor: هذه النون نون العظمة والكبرياء عند العلماء فإن الملوك والعظماء

BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r3.claim: The author explains عرض in its senses of appearing, presenting something, offering goods for sale, or inspecting troops; amāna is the opposite of betrayal and is what has been entrusted.
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r3.anchor: عرض لي أمر كذا أي : ظهر وعرضت له الشيء

BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r4.claim: The first of three levels of trust is the religious and legal obligations, called a trust because they must be received obediently and fulfilled.
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r4.anchor: المرتبة الأولى : أنها التكاليف الشرعية والأمور الدينية المرعية

BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r5.claim: Religious duties are entrusted rights placed with accountable people, who must accept, preserve, and perform them fully.
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r5.anchor: عبر عن التكاليف الشرعية بالأمانة لأنها حقوق مرعية أودعها الله المكلفين

BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r6.claim: This first trust includes intellect, which enables human learning and good action and distinguishes people; it also includes faith and worship, honesty, guarding speech and secrets, repaying debts, fair measures, ritual purity, good prayer, patience, gratitude, vows, chastity, the senses, and all duties required by law.
BURSEVI:v7p193#2/r6.anchor: وتلك الأمانة هي العقل أولا فإن به يحصل تعلم كل ما في طوق البشر

BURSEVI:v7p194/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p194/r1.claim: The primordial covenants were placed in the Black Stone, which is chief among gems and God's custodian of the trust.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r1.anchor: صورة المسمى بالحجر الأسود لسيادته بين الجواهر وألقمه الحق تلك المواثيق

BURSEVI:v7p194/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p194/r2.claim: The second level is divine love, ardor, and attraction, the fruit of the first trust; it distinguishes humans from angels because trials and difficult obligations permit human ascent.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r2.anchor: والمرتبة الثانية : أنها المحبة والعشق والانجذاب الإلهي

BURSEVI:v7p194/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r3.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v7p194/r3.claim: His poem's dark night signifies divine majesty, fear of waves the awe of overpowering attributes, and the whirlpool the frightening trials and barriers in love's sea; angels and ascetics remain lightly burdened at its shore.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r3.anchor: أراد بقوله : "شب تاريك" جلال الذات وبقوله : "بيم موج" خوف صفات القهر

BURSEVI:v7p194/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r4.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v7p194/r4.claim: His other verse says angels do not know the story of love and asks that a cup be poured on Adam's earth.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r4.anchor: فرشته عشق نداندكه يست قصه مخوان

BURSEVI:v7p194/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r5.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v7p194/r5.claim: His couplet says the angels benefit from excellent worship, while the grace of love was poured upon Adam.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r5.anchor: وقول المولى الجامي : ملائك را ه سود

BURSEVI:v7p194/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p194/r6.claim: Lawami says angels lack humanity's painful love and trials; without suffering, love has no worth. Humans bearing the description “corrupting on earth” and “unjust, ignorant” can endure the wine of trial because the heart bears what the body cannot.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r6.anchor: محبت بى دردرا قدر وقيمتى نيست عشق را طائفة در خورند

BURSEVI:v7p194/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p194/r7.claim: The third level is divine effusion without intermediary, which no one owns; it comes through removing existential veils by annihilation in the Reality and subsistence through Lordship, as the fulfillment of love and the level of the divine Essence.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r7.anchor: والمرتبة الثالثة أنها الفيض الإلهي بلا واسطة

BURSEVI:v7p194/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p194/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p194/r8.claim: At this level the heart gives birth to God's deputy on earth who bears the trust; the three levels belong respectively to common people, the elect, and the most elect, with each level's inner core leading to the next.
BURSEVI:v7p194/r8.anchor: وفي هذا المقام يتولد من القلب طفل خليفة الله في الأرض

BURSEVI:v7p195/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195/r1.claim: The author's shaykh said that food has a divine spirit as well as bodily substance; the body and spirit are strengthened together, as the Mathnawi says lawful food increases wisdom, love, and refinement.
BURSEVI:v7p195/r1.anchor: فقال أثناء الإفطار أن لهذا الخبر روحا حقانيا فظاهره يرجع إلى الجسد

BURSEVI:v7p195/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195/r2.claim: Every existent has either an animal or divine spirit; even a dead body retains divine spirit apart from the animal spirit, and all things truly glorify God because life runs through them.
BURSEVI:v7p195/r2.anchor: ولكل موجود روح إما حيواني أو حقاني فجسد الميت له روح حقاني

BURSEVI:v7p195/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195/r3.claim: Examples of this life in creation include mountains praising with David, wind carrying Solomon, earth swallowing Qarun, the Prophet's mosque trunk moaning, and a stone greeting the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v7p195/r3.anchor: ولذا سبح الجبال مع داود وحمل الريح سليمان عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v7p195/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195/r4.claim: The Mathnawi verses chide people for treating beings as lifeless and missing the speech of the world's parts.
BURSEVI:v7p195/r4.anchor: ون شما سوى جمادى مى رويد محرم جان جمادان ون شويد

BURSEVI:v7p195/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195/r5.claim: A second explanation is that God placed reason and understanding in the inanimate things when He offered them the trust, just as He did in Solomon's ant, the hoopoe, animals, stones, trees, and soil; they heard and answered His question about reward for keeping the trust and punishment for betrayal.
BURSEVI:v7p195/r5.anchor: والوجه الثاني أن الله تعالى ركب العقل والفهم في الجمادات المذكورة

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r1.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains refused from fear that they would fail the trust and be punished, not from disobedience; the offer was optional, since obligatory refusal would merit blame, which God did not impose.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r1.anchor: ولم يكن هذا القول منهن من جهة المعصية والمخالفة بل من جهة الخوف

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r2.claim: The mountains said they were subject to divine command and sought neither reward nor punishment; their refusal came from fear of failing the trust, not disobedience.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى وخفن من الأمانة وحملها وقلن يا رب نحن مسخرات بأمرك لا نريد ثوابا ولا عقابا

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r3.claim: An alternative treats the offer as a hypothetical parable: their lack of capacity is pictured as refusal and fear, and the trust's greatness as a heavy physical burden that even enormous self-aware bodies would decline.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r3.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنه محمول على الفرض والتمثيل

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r4.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r4.claim: He distinguishes the mountains' voluntary offer, which they declined, from the human's imposed duty, which he undertook.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r4.anchor: كما قال الإمام القشيري (أمانتها برانها عرض نمود

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r5.claim: Humanity means the human race; it accepted the trust despite weak bodily constitution because carrying it requires resolve, not physical strength.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r5.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس بدليل قوله : {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا}

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r6.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r6.claim: Carrying the trust means either accepting it through innate capacity or acknowledging it at the primordial covenant by saying بلى.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r6.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : وهو إما عبارة عن قبولها بموجب استعداده الفطري

BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r7.claim: The author cites the claim that God carried people on land and sea and that the reward for excellence is excellence; an analogy says weak trees bear the heaviest, sweetest fruit because divine care supports the weak.
BURSEVI:v7p195#2/r7.anchor: قال الله تعالى : {وحملناهم في البر والبحر} (الإسراء : 70) {هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان} (الرحمن : 60)

BURSEVI:v7p197/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r1.speaker: جنيد
BURSEVI:v7p197/r1.claim: Junayd says Adam looked at God's bestowal rather than the trust's burden, so the joy of the gift made him forget its weight; divine grace said that lifting was Adam's choice while preservation was God's.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r1.anchor: شيخ جنيد قدس سره (فرموده كه نظر آدم

BURSEVI:v7p197/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p197/r2.claim: A report says Adam asked whether to carry the trust by his own strength or through God; he was told that whoever bears what comes from God can bear it only through God.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r2.anchor: وروي أن آدم عليه السلام قال : أحمل الأمانة بقوتي أم بالحق

BURSEVI:v7p197/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p197/r3.claim: A Persian verse says that the burden can be borne only with God's help; another says the throne refused it but a human can carry it by divine power.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : آن باركه ازبردن آن عرش ابا كرد

BURSEVI:v7p197/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p197/r4.claim: The human alone was fit to bear this immense trust and the mantle of the earthly vicegerent announced in the creation of Adam; the trust's appointment exposed the envy of the devils.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r4.anchor: خلعت حمل امانت جز برقامت با استقامت انسان

BURSEVI:v7p197/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p197/r5.claim: Humanity is unjust to itself through disobedience and failure to fulfill the trust, and ignorant of the consequences of betraying it.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r5.anchor: لنفسه بمعصية ربه حيث لم يف بالأمانة

BURSEVI:v7p197/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p197/r6.claim: Zulm means putting something outside its proper place by deficiency, excess, or wrong time or location; the author illustrates the term with taking milk too early and digging ground where it should not be dug.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r6.anchor: والظلم وضع الشيء في غير موضعه المختص به إما بنقصان أو بزيادة

BURSEVI:v7p197/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p197/r7.claim: The term applies to small or great transgression, so Adam and Iblis can both be called unjust despite the vast difference between their wrongs.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r7.anchor: ولذا قيل لآدم في تقدمه ظالم وفي إبليس ظالم وإن كان بين الظلمين بون بعيد

BURSEVI:v7p197/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p197/r8.speaker: بعض الحكماء
BURSEVI:v7p197/r8.claim: One classification begins with injustice between a person and God, whose gravest forms are unbelief, shirk, and hypocrisy.
BURSEVI:v7p197/r8.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء : الظلم ثلاثة : أحدهما : بين الإنسان وبين الله

QASHANI:33:72-73/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:72-73/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:72-73/r1.claim: The trust is divine identity deposited in the heavens, earth, and mountains, then concealed by determinations; they lacked capacity, while humans bore it through stronger preparedness and claimed it as their own.
QASHANI:33:72-73/r1.anchor: بإيداع حقيقة الهوية عندها واحتجابها بالتعينات بها

QASHANI:33:72-73/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:72-73/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:72-73/r2.claim: The human is unjust by withholding God's right when displaying self and ignorant because selfhood veils the trust.
QASHANI:33:72-73/r2.anchor: لقوة استعداده واقتداره على حملها فانتحلها لنفسه بإضافتها إليه

QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the trust is God's self-manifestation and attributes deposited according to each creature's capacity; the heavens and earth deliver it by displaying their perfections.
QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r2.anchor: أو عرضنا الأمانة الإلهية بالتجلي عليها وإيداع ما تطيق حملها فيها من الصفات

QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r3.claim: On the alternative, the heavens and earth refused by withholding but ultimately delivered the trust; humanity carried it by concealing perfection through satanic selfhood and blocking ascent in knowledge.
QASHANI:33:72-73#2/r3.anchor: فأبين أن يحملنها بخيانتها وإمساكها عندها والامتناع عن أدائها

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r7.claim: One reading supplies the inhabitants of the heavens, earth, and mountains as those to whom the trust was offered; another says God gave them life and reason, as in the speaking earth and heaven.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r7.anchor: هنا إضمار أي : أهل السموات والأرض والجبال . وقيل أحياها وأعقلها

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r8.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains refused the trust because they feared betraying it, while humanity accepted it and betrayed it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r8.anchor: فأبين أن يحملنها } : أي أبين أن تخن فيها ، { وحملها الإنسان } : أي خان فيها

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r9.claim: One interpretation says unbelievers betray the original trust of knowledge through disbelief, while other people betray it through sins of differing degrees.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r9.anchor: فالكفار خانوا في الأصل الأمانة - وهي المعرفة - فكفروا

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r10.claim: The heavens’ refusal was compassionate fear rather than pride; they sought release from the trust and God excused them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r10.anchor: ويقال ( أبين ) إباء إشفاق لا إباء استكبار ، واستعفين

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r11.claim: Humanity accepted the trust but did not observe it fully, each according to his own measure.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r11.anchor: قبلها ثم ما رعوها حق رعايتها . . كل بقدره

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r12.claim: The trust is interpreted as fulfilling obligations, in their roots and branches.

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r13.claim: Another interpretation defines the trust as monotheism in belief and diligent observance of its limits.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r13.anchor: الأمانة التوحيد عقدا وحفظ الحدود جهدا

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r14.claim: Adam and his descendants carried the trust, which Qushayri links to God honoring humanity in travel and provision as a reward for excellence.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r14.anchor: لما حمل آدم الأمانة وأولاده قال تعالى : { وحملناهم فى البر والبحر }

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r15.claim: Human beings carry the trust through God’s aid, not their own; Adam harmed himself by failing to fear what the heavens and earth feared.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r15.anchor: ويقال حمل الإنسان بالله لا بنفسه . ويقال ظلم نفسه حيث لم يشفق

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r16.claim: The heavens and earth feared God’s manifestation of lordship and grandeur, while Adam and his descendants accepted through the manifestation of divine gentleness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r16.anchor: كاشف السموات والأرض بوصف الربوبية والعظمة فأشفقوا ، وكاشف آدم وذريته بوصف اللطف

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r17.claim: Physical bodies cannot carry the trust; hearts can, and Adam carried it because he possessed inward reality, as a poem says wisdom’s mountains are easier than a shirt.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r17.anchor: والحمل إنما تحمله القلوب . وآدم كان صاحب معنى فحمل

QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r18.claim: Adam aspired to the trust when it was offered, drawing creation’s aspiration away; after they refused, he accepted willingly.
QUSHAYRI:v3p45/r18.anchor: علق آدم بها همته ، فصرف بهمته جميع المخلوقات عنها

SULAMI:v2p151#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r1.claim: People owe one trust to other people and another trust to their Creator.
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أداء أمانة الخلق واداء أمانة الخالق

SULAMI:v2p151#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r2.claim: The trust is realizing divine unity through singling out God alone.
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : الأمانة هي تحقيق التوحيد على سبيل التفريد

SULAMI:v2p151#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r3.claim: He rebukes corrupt people who mishandle the trust, curry rulers, consume forbidden wealth, and ignore the grave consequences of their conduct.
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r3.anchor: قال الحسن البصري : رأيتهم والله قد اشتروا الأمانة بأموالهم ووسعوا لها دورهم

SULAMI:v2p151#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r4.claim: The heavens and earth declined the trust; Adam accepted only after learning that God, not his own strength, would enable its carrying.
SULAMI:v2p151#3/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : إن الإمانة عرضت على السموات والأرض فأبوا حملها

SULAMI:v2p152/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p152/r1.claim: Humanity wrongs itself by imagining that anyone can carry the trust independently, and is ignorant of its gravity and need for divine enabling.
SULAMI:v2p152/r1.anchor: قال : ظلوما حيث ظن أن أحدا يحمل بنفسه شيئا

SULAMI:v2p152/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p152/r2.claim: Trusts apply to the self, heart, secret, innermost heart, spirit, eyes, tongue, hearing, feet, and hands; neglecting them wastes one's time and effort.
SULAMI:v2p152/r2.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : الامانات شتى على النفس أمانة وعلى القلب أمانة وعلى السر أمانة

SULAMI:v2p152/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p152/r3.claim: The heavens and earth declined because they thought they must carry the trust themselves; Adam accepted when he knew God would carry it through him.
SULAMI:v2p152/r3.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : إن الله لما عرض على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبوا حملها

SULAMI:v2p152/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p152/r4.claim: Adam's joy at God's offering made him forget the trust's burden and difficulty, so he accepted without attending to its weight.
SULAMI:v2p152/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : نظر آدم إلى عرض الحق فأنساه لذة العرض ثقل الأمانة وشدتها

SULAMI:v2p152/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p152/r5.claim: The heavens and earth feared the trust's gravity, but its acceptance became easy to Adam because God said it was offered.
SULAMI:v2p152/r5.anchor: وقال أيضا : أشفقت السماوات والأرض عن حمل الأمانة لعظم خطرها وسهل على آدم قبولها

SULAMI:v2p152/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r6.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p152/r6.claim: A person could carry thousands of trusts if God offers the ability to carry them.
SULAMI:v2p152/r6.anchor: وقال : لو كانت مثل الأمانة ألوف أمانات حملتها بعد أن يكون عن عرضك حملها

SULAMI:v2p152/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r7.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p152/r7.claim: Adam was unjust to himself and ignorant of the outcome of accepting the trust.
SULAMI:v2p152/r7.anchor: وقال : في قوله : ﴿ ظلوما جهولا ﴾ ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بعاقبته

SULAMI:v2p152/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p152/r8.claim: Adam wronged himself by failing to fear what the heavens and earth had feared.
SULAMI:v2p152/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ظلم نفسه حيث لم يشفق مما أشفق منه السماوات والأرض

SULAMI:v2p152/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r9.speaker: فارس عن الحسين
SULAMI:v2p152/r9.claim: Creatures and inanimate things fled the trust, assuming they must carry it by themselves; Adam learned that the heart, the locus of God's gaze, bears it through God, while mountains could not bear it.
SULAMI:v2p152/r9.anchor: قال فارس عن الحسين في قوله : ﴿ إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها ﴾

SULAMI:v2p152/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p152/r10.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v2p152/r10.claim: The heart can bear what the body cannot.
SULAMI:v2p152/r10.anchor: وانشد فارس : حملتم القلب ما لا يحمل البدن

SULAMI:v2p153/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p153/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p153/r1.claim: The poem's speaker longs to be among those who seek shelter with the beloved, even if only as an eye to see or an ear to hear them.
SULAMI:v2p153/r1.anchor: يا ليتني كنت أدنى من يلوذ بكم … عينا لأنظركم أم ليتني أذن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r1.claim: The trust means the religious obligations; the heavens, earth, and mountains were offered them with their reward and punishment, then the human accepted.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r2.claim: Some exegetes tell that Adam near death asked whom to appoint after him; told to offer his succession to all creation, he did so and all refused except his children.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p352#6/r2.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: "إن آدم لما حضرته الوفاة

NAHHAS:v3p328/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p328/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p328/r7.claim: عرضنا means displayed or offered, like offering a maiden for sale; the trust and its neglect were shown to the heavens, earth, angels, jinn, and humans.
NAHHAS:v3p328/r7.anchor: ومن حسن ما قيل في معناه أن معنى عرضنا أظهرنا كما تقول عرضت الجارية على البيع

NAHHAS:v3p328/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p328/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p328/r8.claim: The refusal to bear it means refusing the burden of its sin, as in the verse saying people will carry their loads and additional loads.
NAHHAS:v3p328/r8.anchor: فأبين أن يحملنها أي أن يحملن وزرها كما قال

NAHHAS:v3p328/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p328/r9.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v3p328/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says الإنسان refers to disbelievers and hypocrites: they wrong themselves and are ignorant of their Lord; this answer is figurative like “ask the town.”
NAHHAS:v3p328/r9.anchor: قال الحسن يراد به الكافر والمنافق قال ( إنه كان ظلوما ) لنفسه ( جهولا ) بربه

NAHHAS:v3p328/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p328/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p328/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes the trust literally as reward and punishment, displayed to creation; they declined its burden and obeyed their assigned duties, while humans accepted it.
NAHHAS:v3p328/r10.anchor: وفيه جواب آخر على أن يكون حقيقة أنه عرض على السموات والأرض والجبال الأمانة وتضييعها وهي الثواب والعقاب

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the trust is the prescribed duties. The heavens, earth, and mountains declined from fear of failing them, not disobedience, while honoring God's religion; Adam accepted the burden, and being unjust and ignorant means rashly undertaking God's command without knowing its consequences.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما في قوله : انا عرضنا الامانة الاية قال : الامانة ، الفرائض ، عرضها الله على السموات والأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the trust comprises what creatures were commanded to do and forbidden to do, and that the human who carried it was Adam.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : انا عرضنا الامانة على السموات والأرض قال : الامانة : ما امروا به

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r3.claim: An unattributed report says the heavens were offered the trust one after another, followed by earth and mountains.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r3.anchor: ان الله عرض الامانة على السماء الدنيا فابت ، ثم التي تليها حتى فرغ منها ، ثم الأرض ثم الجبال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r4.claim: The same report says Adam accepted the trust between his ears and shoulders, and God gave him sight, eyelids, a tongue, and a covered private part to help him avoid prohibitions.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r4.anchor: فثلاث امرك بهن فانهن لك عون اني جعلت لك بصرا وجعلت لك شفرتين ففضهما ، عن كل شيء نهيتك ، عنه وجعلت لك لسانا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits a narrative in which the heavens, earth, and mountains each say they are already subjugated and will not bear a duty for reward or punishment; Adam accepts, becoming unjust to himself through sin and ignorant of the consequences.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3159/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله ، عنه في الاية قال : بلغني ان الله تعالى لما خلق السموات والأرض والجبال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r1.speaker: زياد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r1.claim: Ziyad ibn Aslam reports that Adam accepted the trust between his ears and shoulders, and God promised help through eyelids, a tongue he could restrain, and clothing to cover his private parts from what God forbade.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r1.anchor: عن زياد بن اسلم في هذه الاية انا عرضنا الامانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فقال الانسان : بين اذني وهاتفي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r2.claim: Mujahid says Adam asked what the trust was and was told that good conduct would earn reward and wrongdoing punishment; Adam accepted, then disobeyed within the short interval from noon to afternoon.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله ، عنه في الاية قال : لما خلق الله السموات والأرض والجبال ، عرض الامانة عليهن فلم يقبلوها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r3.speaker: ابن اضشوع
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r3.claim: Ibn al-Adshu' reports that the creatures were offered deeds and their rewards, groaned for three days and nights, and said they lacked capacity for the deeds and did not want the reward.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r3.anchor: عن ابن اضشوع في الاية قال : عرض عليهن العمل وجعل لهن الثواب فضججن ثلاثة ايام ولياليهن ، فقلن : ربنا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says that part of the trust is a woman being entrusted to guard her chastity.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3160/r4.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله ، عنه قال : من الامانة ان ائتمنت المراة على فرجها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud interprets the trust as financial deposits; another report from him extends it to all duties while treating financial trust as the greatest instance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r1.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود هي أمانات المال كالودائع ونحوها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r2.claim: The majority take the trust as everything entrusted to a person, religious or worldly, including commands and prohibitions; the whole law is a trust.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r2.anchor: وذهبت فرقة، هي الجمهور، إلى أنه كل شيء يؤتمن الإنسان عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r3.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb includes a woman's chastity among the trusts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r3.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب من الأمانة أن ائتمنت المرأة على فرجها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r4.claim: Abu al-Darda says ritual bathing after sexual impurity is a trust.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء غسل الجنابة أمانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r5.claim: The offer asked the great creatures to bear duties with reward for obedience and punishment for failure; they declined in fear, either through awareness God created in them or by addressing the angels within them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية إنا عرضنا على هذه المخلوقات العظام أن تحمل الأوامر والنواهي وتقتضي الثواب إن أحسنت والعقاب إن أساءت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r6.claim: A report says the creatures asked to remain subject to God's will, obeying without being left to their own judgment or seeking reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r6.anchor: ويروى أنها قالت «رب ذرني مسخرة لما شئت أتيت طائعة فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r7.claim: They say the human accepted responsibility for the trust and was unjust to himself and ignorant of its magnitude.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r7.anchor: وحمل الإنسان الأمانة أي التزم القيام بحقها، وهو في ذلك ظلوم لنفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r8.claim: Al-Hasan interprets carrying the trust as betraying it and applies the verse to the unbeliever and hypocrite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن حملها معناه خان فيها والآية في الكافر والمنافق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r9.claim: The degree of blame among sinful believers varies according to their conduct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r9.anchor: قال الفقيه الإمام القاضي: والعصاة على قدرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r10.claim: They identify the human as Adam, who accepted the trust, was promised reward for good and punishment for evil, and disobeyed within the same day, losing Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك وغيره الإنسان آدم تحمل الأمانة فما تم له يوم حتى عصى المعصية التي أخرجته من الجنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r11.claim: They also identify the human as Adam's son Cain, who had promised his father to guard the family while Adam traveled to Mecca.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن مسعود الإنسان ابن آدم قابيل الذي قتل أخاه وكان قد تحمل الأمانة لأبيه أن يحفظ الأهل بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r12.claim: Some say al-insān means humankind generally; the author considers this apt because the trust itself is universal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم الإنسان النوع كله وهذا حسن مع عموم الأمانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r13.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the creatures fulfilled their duties and declined the blame of disobedience, while humans accepted the blame attached to God's commands and law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402/r13.anchor: وقال الزجاج معنى الآية إنا عرضنا الأمانة في نواهينا وأوامرنا على هذه المخلوقات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r1.claim: On the majority interpretation, 41:11 describes a response to a direct command, while this verse describes refusal of an offered choice, so the passages are consistent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r1.anchor: وتستقيم هذه الآية مع قوله تعالى: أتينا طائعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r2.claim: A report says the creatures refused the trust, but Adam accepted it between his ears and shoulders; God promised to protect his sight and modesty from the unlawful.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r2.anchor: وروي أن الله تعالى عرض الأمانة على هذه المخلوقات فأبت، فلما عرضها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r3.claim: The author omits further details of that report because they are not reliable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r3.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى أشياء تركتها اختصارا لعدم صحتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r4.claim: Some take the scene as metaphor: comparing the trust's burden with the creatures' capacity shows they could not bear it, as when one tests whether a beast can carry a load.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p402#2/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: إن الآية من المجاز، أي إنا إذا قايسنا ثقل الأمانة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, and also Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interpret the trust as the prescribed duties offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains, then accepted by Adam with their burden of reward or punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r1.anchor: أنها الفرائض عرضها الله على السماوات والأرض والجبال إن أدتها أثابها وإن ضيعتها عذبها فكرهت ذلك وعرضها على آدم فقبلها بما فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Adam accepted the trust, but sinned before sunset on the same day, between the afternoon prayer and sunset.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r2.anchor: وكذلك قال سعيد بن جبير عرضت الأمانة على آدم فقيل له تأخذها بما فيها إن أطعت غفرت لك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r3.speaker: قتادة والضحاك والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r3.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and the majority likewise take the trust to mean the prescribed duties.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r3.anchor: وممن ذهب إلى أنها الفرائض قتادة والضحاك والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r4.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī reports that when Adam went on pilgrimage, heaven and earth and mountains refused his request to guard his children; Qābīl agreed, then killed Hābīl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r4.anchor: روى السدي عن أشياخه أن آدم لما أراد الحج قال للسماء احفظي ولدي بالأمانة فأبت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة عن بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r5.claim: A report from some exegetes says Adam, near death, was told to offer his succession to all creation; they all refused except his child.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r5.anchor: وحكى ابن قتيبة عن بعض المفسرين ان آدم لما حضرته الوفاة قال يا رب من أستخلف من بعدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r6.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r6.claim: Most exegetes say God endowed the heavens, earth, and mountains with reason and speech; they refused from fear, since the offer was a choice, and feared failing it and being punished.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r6.anchor: أن الله تعالى ركب العقل في هذه الأعيان وأفهمهن خطابه وأنطقهن بالجواب حين عرضها عليهن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the offer as addressed to the inhabitants of the heavens, earth, and mountains, meaning the angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r7.anchor: أن المراد بالآية إنا عرضنا الأمانة على أهل السماوات وأهل الأرض وأهل الجبال من الملائكة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r8.claim: The majority identify the human who bore the trust as Adam.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the human who bore the trust as Qābīl.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the human as the unbeliever and hypocrite.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r11.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p427#2/r11.claim: Thaʿlab identifies the human as all people.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the person was unjust to himself and heedless of his Lord’s command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r1.anchor: ظلوما لنفسه غرا بأمر ربه قاله ابن عباس والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r2.claim: Mujāhid says he wronged himself and was ignorant of the outcome of his action.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r2.anchor: ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بعاقبة امره قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib says he wronged himself by disobeying his Lord and was ignorant of the trust’s punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r3.anchor: ظلوما بمعصية ربه جهولا بعقاب الأمانة قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj offers a reading he says accords with tafsir: God entrusted humanity with obedience and the heavens, earth, and mountains with submission; they fulfilled it, while whoever sins bears the trust as a burden. He cites 41:11 and other signs of creation’s submission.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r4.anchor: إن الله تعالى ائتمن بني آدم على ما افترضه عليهم من طاعته وائتمن السماوات والأرض والجبال على طاعته والخضوع له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan likewise takes the bearer as the unbeliever and hypocrite who betrayed the trust; the obedient person is not called unjust and ignorant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p429/r5.anchor: فأما من أطاع فلا يقال كان ظلوما جهولا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r1.claim: Al-Awfi reports that the trust is obedience, offered to heaven, earth, and mountains before Adam; they could not bear it, while Adam accepted after hearing of reward and punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r1.anchor: يعني بالأمانة: الطاعة، وعرضها عليهم قبل أن يعرضها على آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r2.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talha reports that the trust is obligatory duties; creation feared failing them out of reverence for God’s religion, while Adam accepted, rashly trusting himself with God’s charge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r2.anchor: الأمانة: الفرائض، عرضها الله على السموات والأرض والجبال، إن أدوها أثابهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam accepted on promise of forgiveness for obedience and punishment for disobedience, then sinned before that day ended; Ibn Kathir questions a similar disconnected report from al-Dahhak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r3.anchor: فما كان إلا قدر ما بين العصر إلى الليل من ذلك اليوم، حتى أصاب الخطيئة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r4.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك والحسن البصري وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r4.claim: These authorities call the trust obligatory duties; others say obedience, and Ibn Kathir reconciles them as responsibility for commands and prohibitions with reward or punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r4.anchor: وهكذا قال مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، والضحاك، والحسن البصري، وغير واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r5.claim: Ubayy includes a woman’s sexual chastity among the trusts placed in her care.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r5.anchor: من الأمانة أن المرأة اؤتمنت على فرجها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r6.claim: Qatada defines the trust as religion, obligatory duties, and limits.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: الأمانة: الدين والفرائض والحدود.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r7.speaker: بعضهم ومالك عن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r7.claim: Some specify ritual washing after sexual impurity; Zayd ibn Aslam lists prayer, fasting, and that washing as three trusts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r7.anchor: الأمانة ثلاثة: الصلاة، والصوم، والاغتسال من الجنابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r8.claim: All definitions converge on religious responsibility: accept commands and prohibitions, earning reward by fulfilling them and punishment by neglect; humanity accepted despite weakness, ignorance, and injustice, save whom God guides.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p488/r8.anchor: وكل هذه الأقوال لا تنافي بينها، بل هي (3) متفقة وراجعة إلى أنها التكليف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r1.claim: Hasan describes the trust, with its reward and punishment, being offered to seven heavens, the Throne’s bearers, seven earths, and towering mountains; each declines.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r1.anchor: عرضها على السبع الطباق الطرائق التي زينت بالنجوم، وحملة العرش العظيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r2.claim: Muqatil says God assembled creation and offered obedience as the trust; heavens and earths declined as unable, but Adam accepted reward and punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p489/r2.anchor: فبدأ بالسموات فعرض عليهن الأمانة وهي الطاعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r1.claim: Mujahid depicts heaven, earth, and mountains declining duties because they already bear their inhabitants and do not seek reward; Adam’s burden is blameworthy in its outcome.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r1.anchor: عرضها على السموات فقالت: يا رب، حملتني الكواكب وسكان السماء وما ذكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r2.speaker: ابن أشوع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r2.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains groaned to God for three days and nights, saying they lacked capacity and did not seek reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r2.anchor: ضججن إلى الله ثلاثة أيام ولياليهن، وقلن: ربنا. لا طاقة لنا بالعمل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم وأبو حازم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r3.claim: Adam accepted the trust between his ears and shoulders; God promised help restraining the eyes, tongue, and private parts when tempted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r3.anchor: فقال الإنسان: بين أذني وعاتقي فقال الله تعالى (6) : إني معينك عليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the trust involved religious duties and reward or punishment; after Adam agreed, God promised eyelids, a tongue gate, and covering for the genitals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490/r4.anchor: أما إذ تحملت هذا فسأعينك، أجعل لبصرك حجابا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r1.speaker: الحكم بن عمير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r1.claim: A very rare report says trust and fidelity descended with prophets; revelation explained duties in every language, then trust and covenants were withdrawn from hearts while scripture remained. Ibn Kathir calls it very rare but says it has corroboration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r1.anchor: إن الأمانة والوفاء نزلا على ابن آدم مع الأنبياء، فأرسلوا به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r2.claim: Five deeds alongside faith lead to Paradise: keep the five prayers, give zakat willingly, fast Ramadan, perform pilgrimage if able, and fulfill trust; Abu al-Darda explains the last as ghusl after sexual impurity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p490#2/r2.anchor: خمس من جاء بهن يوم القيامة مع إيمان دخل الجنة: من حافظ على الصلوات الخمس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r1.claim: Martyrdom atones for sins except breach of trust; its bearer must retrieve it from Hell, carry it to the brink, and may fall eternally if it slips. Trust includes fasting, ablution, speech, especially deposits; al-Bara confirms Ibn Masud’s account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r1.anchor: القتل في سبيل الله يكفر الذنوب كلها -أو قال: يكفر كل شيء -إلا الأمانة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r2.claim: A second route gives the same warning but omits the extension to prayer and everything; Ibn Kathir calls its chain good though canonical collections omit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r2.anchor: عن (13) عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنحوه. ولم يذكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r3.speaker: حذيفة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r3.claim: Trust descended into hearts, followed by Quran and Sunnah, then is withdrawn in stages, leaving a scorched trace; people scarcely keep trust and admired men may lack even a mustard seed of faith. Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p491/r3.anchor: أن الأمانة نزلت في جذر (3) قلوب الرجال، ثم نزل القرآن فعلموا من القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r1.claim: Four virtues suffice against worldly loss: guard trust, speak truth, show good character, and eat lawfully.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r1.anchor: أربع إذا كن فيك فلا عليك ما فاتك من الدنيا: حفظ أمانة، وصدق حديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r2.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits the same four qualities from Ibn Umar, adding Ibn Hujayra in its chain and assigning it to Ibn Umar.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r2.anchor: فزاد في الإسناد: "ابن حجيرة"، وجعله من (12) مسند ابن عمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r3.speaker: زياد بن حدير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r3.claim: Ziyad wept when a companion swore by trust; he explained that Umar strongly forbade oaths by trust.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r3.anchor: كان عمر بن الخطاب ينهى عن الحلف بالأمانة أشد النهي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r4.speaker: بريدة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r4.claim: Whoever swears by trust is not one of the community; Abu Dawud alone reports this marfu hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p492/r4.anchor: من حلف بالأمانة فليس منا"، تفرد به أبو داود

JISHUMI:v8p5771#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5771#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5771#2/r3.claim: Amānah is a binding contract that must be fulfilled.

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r1.claim: Believers fulfill the trust and merit mercy; God forgives the repentant and shows mercy to believers.
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r1.anchor: وأما المؤمن والمؤمنة فأديا الأمانة، واستوجبا الرحمة

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r4.claim: Angels do not disobey; disobedience is characteristic of humans and jinn.
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن الملائكة لم تعص وأن العصيان عادة الإنس والجن

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r5.claim: The presentation of the trust to the heavens and earth is figurative or addressed to their inhabitants; literal presentation to inanimate things is impossible.
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r5.anchor: المراد بالعرض على أهلها أو التمثيل، فأما العرض على الجماد فمحال

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r6.claim: The presentation describes the state and obligation, not a free choice: God obligates a servant when it is beneficial, without coercing him.
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r6.anchor: وقد بينا أنه بيان الحال والتكليف، فأما التخيير فلا

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r7.claim: “They refused to carry it” cannot mean meritorious refusal of God's command, which would be disbelief; the author instead says they betrayed the trust while bearing its burden.
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r7.anchor: المراد خانوا فيها إذ حملوا وزرها

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r8.claim: Some say the offer was a choice and the heavens asked for relief from the threat; the author's earlier account is preferable because human welfare is not left to their choice.
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r8.anchor: وما قدمناه أولى؛ لأن المصالح لا تقف على اختيارهم

JISHUMI:v8p5775/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5775/r9.claim: Human speech, deeds, sins, carrying the trust, hypocrisy, disbelief, and faith are people's own acts rather than God's creation, making commands, prohibitions, promise, and threat coherent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r1.claim: The trust is God's commands to obey and prohibitions against disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r1.anchor: ما أمر الله سبحانه من طاعته ونهى عن معصيته , قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r2.claim: They identify the trust with the rules and rulings God imposed on people, close in meaning to obedience and restraint.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r2.anchor: القوانين والأحكام التي أوجبها الله على العباد وهو قريب من الأول , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد , والحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r3.speaker: أبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r3.claim: He identifies it as entrusting men and women with sexual chastity; a reported address to Adam calls his sexual organ a trust to be used only lawfully.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r3.anchor: هي ائتمان الرجال والنساء على الفروج ، قاله أبي . وقيل إن أول ما خلق الله من آدم الفرج

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r4.claim: The trust is what people entrust to one another; its first breach was Cain's betrayal of Adam's trust by murdering Abel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r4.anchor: الأمانات التي يأتمن الناس بعضهم بعضا عليها وأولها ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r5.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r5.claim: He says creation was entrusted with signs of God's lordship, which all displayed except the human who concealed and denied them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r5.anchor: ما أودعه الله في السموات والأرض والجبال والخلق من الدلائل على ربوبيته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r6.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r6.claim: One account takes the offer as a command to preserve the trust, with grave sin attached to wasting it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r6.anchor: عرضها هو الأمر بما يجب من حفظها وعظم المأثم في تضييعها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r7.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r7.claim: He says the trust was weighed against the heavens, earth, and mountains, proved heavier, and overwhelmed them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r7.anchor: الأمانة عورضت بالسموات والأرض والجبال فكانت أثقل منها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r8.claim: A third explanation is that the trust was offered so acceptance would follow informed knowledge of its demands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r8.anchor: أن الله عرض حملها ليكون الدخول فيها بعد العلم بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r9.claim: They say the offer was made to the heavens, earth, and mountains themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r9.anchor: أنها عرضت على السموات والأرض والجبال ، قاله ابن عباس ، ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r10.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r10.claim: He says the offer was made to the inhabitants of the heavens, earth, and mountains, namely angels and people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r10.anchor: عرضت على أهل السموات وأهل الأرض وأهل الجبال من الملائكة قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r11.claim: Their refusal may signify incapacity and fear, or caution about falling short.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r11.anchor: أبين أن يحملنها عجزا وأشفقن منها خوفا . الثاني : أبين أن يحملنها حذرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r12.speaker: ثعلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r12.claim: He identifies the human who carried the trust as humanity collectively.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r13.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r13.claim: Alternatively, Adam carried it and it then passed to his descendants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r13.anchor: أنه آدم ثم انتقلت منه إلى ولده , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r14.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r14.claim: He reports that the heavens, earth, and mountains declined after learning they would be rewarded for good and punished for evil; Adam accepted that bargain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r14.anchor: الحسن أن الأمانة لما عرضت على السموات والأرض والجبال قالت : وما فيها ؟ قيل لها : إن أحسنت جزيت وإن أسأت عوقبت فقالت : لا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r15.claim: He recounts that Adam accepted after hearing the same reward-and-punishment terms, and carried the trust only briefly before leaving the Garden.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r15.anchor: قال مجاهد : فلما خلق الله آدم عرضها عليه قال : وما هي ؟ قال : { إن أحسنت آجرتك وإن أسأت عذبتك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r16.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r16.claim: He explains the human as unjust to himself and ignorant of his Lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r16.anchor: ظلوما لنفسه , جهولا بربه , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r17.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r17.claim: He describes the human as unjust in his offense and ignorant about the burden inherited by his descendants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r17.anchor: ظلوما في خطيئته , جهولا فيما حمل ولده من بعده , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r18.claim: He says the human wronged the trust; Ibn Jurayj glosses ignorance as not knowing the outcome.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p428/r18.anchor: ظلوما لحقها , قاله قتادة . جهولا بعاقبة أمره , قاله ابن جريج

MUQATIL:33:72-73/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:72-73/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:72-73/r1.claim: The trust is obedience carrying reward and punishment: the heavens, earth, and mountains refused from fear of punishment, while Adam accepted after learning its terms and soon sinned; the human is Adam, unjust to himself and ignorant of the consequence.
MUQATIL:33:72-73/r1.anchor: { إنا عرضنا الأمانة } وهى الطاعة { على السماوات والأرض والجبال } على الثواب والعقاب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r1.claim: The trust means obedience to God; its bearer is called treacherous until it is returned to its owner, like a burden of debt carried on someone.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r1.anchor: وهو يريد بالأمانة الطاعة لله ويحمل الأمانة الخيانة يقال فلان حامل للامانة ومحتمل لها أى لا يؤديها إلى صاحبها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r2.claim: The vast heavens, earth, and mountains submit to God's will in the way fitting inanimate beings, obeying His creative acts and diverse arrangements.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r2.anchor: قد انقادت لأمر الله انقياد مثلها وهو ما يتأتى من الجمادات واطاعت له الطاعة التى تليق بها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r3.claim: God also says the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and animals prostrate, and that some stones fall in awe.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r3.anchor: أن الشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب يسجدون لله وأن من الحجارة لما يهبط من خشية الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r4.claim: Unlike inanimate creation, humans can obey and submit as accountable rational beings; refusing the trust means betraying it rather than merely declining a physical burden.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r4.anchor: وأما الإنسان فلم تكن حاله فيما يصح منه من الطاعة ويليق به من الانقياد لأوامر الله ونواهيه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r5.claim: On this reading, the heavens and mountains refused treachery, while humanity took on the trust by failing to discharge it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r5.anchor: ﴿ فأبين أن يحملنها ﴾ أى أبين الخيانة فيها وأن لا يؤدينها ﴿ وأشفقن منها ﴾ وخفن من الخيانة فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r6.claim: Humanity is unjust by neglecting the trust and ignorant by missing its own good despite being able to fulfill it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r6.anchor: ﴿ إنه كان ظلوما ﴾ لكونه تاركا لاداء الامانة ﴿ جهولا ﴾ لاخطائه ما يسعده مع تمكه منه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r7.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says unbelievers and hypocrites carried the trust by betraying it, but obedient prophets and believers cannot be called unjust and ignorant.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج الكافر والمنافق حملا الامانة أى خانا ولم يطيعا ومن أطاع من الأنبياء والمؤمنين فلا يقال كان ظلوما جهولا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r8.claim: An alternative says the trust was so immense that the greatest created bodies refused it in awe, while weak humanity carried it and then betrayed its guarantee; the Arabic idiom compares this to fat being asked where it goes and answering that it straightens a crooked thing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p317#5/r8.anchor: وقيل معنى الآية أن ما كلفه الإنسان بلغ من عظمة أنه عرض على أعظم ما خلق الله من الاجرام

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r1.claim: After setting out legal rulings in the surah, God commands compliance; the amanah, by the sound majority view, encompasses all duties of religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r1.anchor: والأمانة تعم جميع وظائف الدين على الصحيح من الأقوال

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmits Ibn Abbas's report that God offered Adam the trust: carrying it earns reward and neglecting it brings punishment; Adam accepted, and after a short stay in Paradise was expelled by Satan.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r2.anchor: إن حملتها أجرت وإن ضيعتها عذبت فاحتملها بما فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r3.claim: The trust consists of the obligatory duties God entrusted to people.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r3.anchor: فالأمانة هي الفرائض التي ائتمن الله عليها العباد

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the trust includes financial deposits; another report from him says all obligations, especially property entrusted to others.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r4.anchor: هي في أمانات الأموال كالودائع وغيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb identifies a woman's chastity as one of the trusts.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r5.anchor: من الأمانة أن ائتمنت المرأة على فرجها

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r6.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says the major ablution after sexual impurity is a trust, the only aspect of religion in which God entrusted the human being.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r7.claim: A prophetic report calls prayer a trust, since a person may honestly say either that he prayed or that he did not; the same applies to fasting and major ablution.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r7.anchor: وفي حديث مرفوع: " الأمانة الصلاة " إن شئت قلت قد صليت

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAmr says the sexual organ was God's first trust placed in a person, then lists the ear, eye, tongue, belly, hand, and foot as trusts; without trustworthiness there is no faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r8.anchor: فالفرج أمانة، والأذن أمانة، والعين أمانة

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r9.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r9.claim: Al-Suddī explains the trust through Adam leaving Cain responsible for his family while he visited the House at Mecca; the heavens, earth, and mountains declined, but Cain agreed and then killed his brother.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r9.anchor: وقال السدي هي ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل على ولده وأهله

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r10.claim: Maʿmar transmits al-Ḥasan's report: when told good performance earned reward and failure incurred punishment, the heavens, earth, and mountains refused the trust.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r10.anchor: إن أحسنت جوزيت وإن أسأت عوقبت

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r11.claim: Mujāhid says the trust was offered to Adam after his creation; he accepted responsibility for reward or punishment, and left Paradise within the span from noon to afternoon.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73/r11.anchor: فما كان بين أن تحملها إلى أن أخرج من الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the trust as religious duties: the heavens, earth, and mountains declined from reverence and concern that they could not fulfill them, not from disobedience, while Adam accepted.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r1.anchor: وروى علي ابن طلحة عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r2.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says Ibn Abbas's interpretation is the one followed by exegetes.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r2.anchor: وهذا القول هو الذي عليه أهل التفسير

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r3.claim: Another report says that when Adam neared death, he offered the trust to creation and only his sons accepted it.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r3.anchor: لما حضرت آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم الوفاة أمر أن يعرض الأمانة على الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r4.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r4.claim: Some theologians define the trust as the evidence of God's lordship deposited in the heavens, earth, and mountains: they display it, while the human conceals and denies it.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r4.anchor: من الدلائل على ربوبيته أن يظهروها فأظهروها

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r5.claim: Here ʿaraḍnā means we made apparent, as when a woman is presented for sale; the trust and its neglect were presented to the inhabitants of heaven and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى «عرضنا» أظهرنا، كما تقول: عرضت الجارية على البيع

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r6.claim: The heavens' refusal to bear the trust means refusing to carry its burden or guilt, as in the verse about bearing their burdens.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r6.anchor: { فأبين أن يحملنها } أي أن يحملن وزرها

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the human who took the trust was the unbeliever and hypocrite, unjust to himself and ignorant of his Lord; this is figurative, like asking a town.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r7.anchor: قال الحسن: المراد الكافر والمنافق. { إنه كان ظلوما } لنفسه { جهولا } بربه

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation says the trust and its consequences of reward and punishment were shown to the heavens; they declined out of awe, saying they could not bear it, yet remained obedient to God's other commands.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r9.claim: On the literal account, inanimate beings would need to be given life in order to understand and answer; the offer was voluntary choice for them but binding obligation for humanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r9.anchor: وهذا العرض عرض تخيير لا إلزام. والعرض على الإنسان إلزام

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r10.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r10.claim: Al-Qaffāl and others read the scene as a parable: even the enormous heavens, earth, and mountains could not bear the weight of religious obligations with reward and punishment, yet the unjust, ignorant human undertook them.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#2/r10.anchor: العرض في هذه الآية ضرب مثل

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r1.claim: The parable resembles the mountain passage in al-Ḥashr, followed by the statement that God presents such parables to people.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r1.anchor: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#3/r2.claim: Another figurative reading compares the burden of the trust with the capacity of the heavens and earth; they would refuse if able to speak, just as one says a camel refused a load after comparing its strength with the burden.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r1.claim: One reading takes ʿaraḍnā as weighing the trust against the heavens, earth, and mountains; they were too weak, and the trust outweighed them.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r1.anchor: وقيل: «عرضنا» بمعنى عارضنا الأمانة بالسموات والأرض والجبال فضعفت هذه الأشياء

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r2.claim: An alternative story says Adam presented the trust to the heavens, earth, and mountains when seeking a successor; they refused from fear of its consequences, but his child accepted.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن عرض الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال إنما كان من آدم عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r3.claim: In that story, Adam had been entrusted with earthly creatures and divine commands, then was told to present the trust with reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r3.anchor: وسلطه على جميع ما في الأرض من الأنعام والطير والوحش، وعهد إليه عهدا أمره فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r4.claim: The human is unjust to himself and ignorant of the consequence of what he undertook.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r4.anchor: «إنه كان ظلوما» لنفسه «جهولا» بعاقبة ما تقلد لربه

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim rejects the Adam-at-death story as unsupported by reports and the verse's wording; it does not explain why animals or mountains would be assigned legal commands.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r5.anchor: قال الترمذي الحكيم أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي: عجبت من هذا القائل من أين أتى بهذه القصة!

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that God embodied the trust as a rock; cosmic creatures declined it, while a human volunteered, carried it after warnings, and bore it for his descendants.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r6.anchor: عن عامر الشعبي عن مسروق عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: لما خلق الله الأمانة مثلها صخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r7.claim: In Ibn Masʿud's report, the trust carries reward and punishment, explaining the heavens', earth's, and mountains' fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#4/r7.anchor: إن هذه «الأمانة»، ولها ثواب وعليها عقاب قالوا: يا رب، لا طاقة لنا بها

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r1.claim: Carrying the trust means taking responsibility for its due, thereby wronging oneself.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r1.anchor: أي التزم القيام بحقها، وهو في ذلك ظلوم لنفسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r2.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس وابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r2.claim: Qatadah says the human was ignorant of the trust's scale; Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr are said to share this interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: للأمانة، جهول بقدر ما دخل فيه. وهذا تأويل ابن عباس وابن جبير.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the human was ignorant of his Lord and that carrying the trust means betraying it.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: جهول بربه. قال: ومعنى «حملها» خان فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r4.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj applies the betrayal reading to unbelievers, hypocrites, and sinners according to their degrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: والآية في الكافر والمنافق والعصاة على قدرهم على هذا التأويل.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, his associates, and al-Dahhak identify the human as Adam, who disobeyed within a day and was expelled from Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأصحابه والضحاك وغيره: «الإنسان» آدم، تحمل الأمانة فما تم له يوم

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r6.claim: A report has Adam accept the trust after hearing its consequences; God promises safeguards against forbidden sights and sexual exposure.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن الله تعالى قال له: أتحمل هذه الأمانة بما فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r7.claim: The author prefers humankind generally as the human, which fits the trust's universal scope.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: «الإنسان» النوع كله. وهذا حسن مع عموم الأمانة كما ذكرناه أولا.

QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r8.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r8.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the human as Cain; the author leaves the matter to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:72-73#5/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: الإنسان قابيل. فالله أعلم.

SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r1.claim: عرضنا may describe a real event or use personification and imaginative representation.
SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r1.anchor: وقوله: { إنا عرضنا }: إما حقيقة، وإما تمثيل وتخييل

SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r2.claim: The feminine pronoun in فأبين is permitted for a nonrational broken plural, even though such a plural may be masculine; this avoids supposing the feminine heavens overrode masculine mountains.
SAMIN-DURR:33:72/r2.anchor: أتى بضمير هذه كضمير الإناث؛ لأن جمع التكسير غير العاقل يجوز فيه ذلك، وإن كان مذكرا

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r1.claim: The trust is the burden of moral responsibility, which requires acting against one’s natural disposition; unlike humans, the heavens, earth, and mountains remain as created.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r1.anchor: أي التكليف وهو الأمر بخلاف ما في الطبيعة

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r2.claim: Angels do receive commands and prohibitions, but obedience is congenial to their nature, as eating and drinking are to humans; they glorify God without tiring.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r2.anchor: فيسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون كما يشتغل الإنسان بأمر موافق لطبعه

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r3.claim: One interpretation calls the trust moral responsibility: the negligent incur liability and the faithful receive honor.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r3.anchor: من قال هو التكليف وسمي أمانة لأن من قصر فيه / فعليه الغرامة

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r4.claim: A second interpretation identifies the trust as the declaration that there is no god but God, but al-Razi rejects it because the heavens, earth, and mountains already proclaim divine oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r4.anchor: ومنهم من قال هو قول لا إله إلا الله وهو بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r5.claim: Other interpretations identify the trust with the body’s entrusted organs, or with knowledge of God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r5.anchor: ومنهم من قال الأعضاء فالعين أمانة ينبغي أن يحفظها والأذن كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r6.claim: The “offering” may be literal presentation, resurrection, or comparison in which the trust is weighed against the heavens and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r6.anchor: في العرض وجوه منهم من قال المراد العرض ومنهم من قال الحشر ومنهم من قال المقابلة

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r7.claim: “The heavens and earth” may mean those entities themselves or their inhabitants, with the latter reading supplying an omitted “people of.”
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r7.anchor: أن المراد هي بأعيانها ، والثاني : المراد أهلوها

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r8.claim: The creation’s refusal differs from Iblis’s refusal: prostration was obligatory but the trust was offered, and Iblis acted arrogantly whereas creation humbly feared its incapacity.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#2/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أن هناك السجود كان فرضا ، وههنا الأمانة كانت عرضا

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r1.claim: The trust inspires fear because it resembles a precious, fragile object: one might refuse to accept it for fear of losing it; moral responsibility is both valuable and vulnerable.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r1.anchor: أن يكون عزيزا صعب الحفظ كالأواني من الجواهر التي تكون عزيزة سريعة الانكسار

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r2.claim: It also resembles keeping a deposit during a dangerous time: Satan and his forces were attacking those made morally responsible after Adam left the garden.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r2.anchor: والأمر كان كذلك لأن الشيطان وجنوده كانوا في قصد المكلفين إذ الغرض كان بعد خروج آدم من الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r3.claim: It further resembles custody of animals that need food, water, and care; unlike goods safely set in a box, moral responsibility requires continuing cultivation.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r3.anchor: والتكليف كذلك فإنه يحتاج إلى تربية وتنمية

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r4.claim: One answer says the human accepted the trust from ignorance of its consequences, whereas the heavens and earth knew what it contained; this explains “unjust and ignorant.”
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r4.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى : { إنه كان ظلوما جهولا }

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r5.claim: A second answer says the created things saw their weakness, while the human focused on the trustworthy Lord’s knowledge and power and trusted that He would guard what He entrusted.
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r5.anchor: والثاني : أن الأشياء نظرت إلى أنفسهن فرأين ضعفهن فامتنعن ، والإنسان نظر

RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p202#3/r6.claim: The human’s trust rests on the conviction expressed in “You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”
