STUDYQURAN:33:72/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r1.speaker: Q, Sy
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r1.claim: The Trust is understood as the dictates of faith and belief, as expressed in a famous saying that one without trust has no belief.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r1.anchor: The Trust is understood as relating to the dictates of faith and belief, as in a famous saying

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r2.speaker: IK, Ṭ, Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r2.claim: Many commentators identify the Trust with obedience.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r2.anchor: Many relate the Trust to obedience (IK, Ṭ, Ṭs, Z)

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r3.speaker: IJ, JJ, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r3.claim: Most commentators take the Trust to mean the religious obligations (farāʾiḍ).
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r3.anchor: understood by most as a reference to the requirements

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the Trust to refer to prayer alone.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r4.anchor: though others see it as a reference to prayer alone (Q)

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r5.speaker: IJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r5.claim: The Trust can concern management of each faculty, including tongue, eye, stomach, and sexual parts; this view is linked to 8:27.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r5.anchor: The Trust can also be understood as pertaining to the manner in which one manages each aspect of one’s being

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r6.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r6.claim: Another view sees the Trust as inner faith and outward performance of religion’s requirements.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r6.anchor: It is also said that the Trust pertains to faith inwardly and performing the requirements of religion outwardly (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r7.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r7.claim: The Trust may be the primordial tawḥīd covenant and testimony to God’s Lordship made with all humanity before earthly life.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r7.anchor: the pact or covenant of tawḥīd (Divine Oneness) and the witness to God’s Lordship made with all of humanity

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r8.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r8.claim: Many commentators understand the Trust’s offer to the heavens, earth, and mountains literally.

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r9.speaker: R, Ṭs, Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r9.claim: Another view says the offer was made to their inhabitants: all people of earth, jinn, and angels.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r9.anchor: offered to their inhabitants (R), that is, to all the people of the earth, the jinn, and the angels (Ṭs, Ṭū)

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r10.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains refused because they shrank from a burden they knew was too heavy, not from defiance.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r10.anchor: They refused to bear it not out of defiance, but because they shrank from what they knew to be too heavy a burden

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r11.speaker: Bḍ, IJ, IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r11.claim: Many say they chose passive obedience because accountability entails possible reward and punishment.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r11.anchor: they knew they would be subject to reward and punishment and thus chose to remain passively obedient

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r12.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r12.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains recognized their weakness, while humans understood their station and accepted responsibility as rational beings fit for religious obligations.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r12.anchor: human beings realized their place and assumed their responsibility (R) as creatures possessing intellect and thus fit to observe the obligations of religion (Z)

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r13.speaker: Q, Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r13.claim: A metaphorical interpretation says that despite their size and grandeur, the heavens, earth, and mountains lack capacity for revealed laws, as 59:21 illustrates.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r13.anchor: as in 59:21: Had We made this Quran descend upon a mountain, thou wouldst have seen it humbled

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r14.claim: Humanity’s unique responsibility is to remain in tawḥīd and follow the practices of its religious laws.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r14.anchor: That man bore it thus indicates the unique responsibility human beings bear to remain in a state of tawḥīd

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r15.claim: Breaking that duty breaches humanity’s pre-world covenant with God and violates its true nature.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r15.anchor: they break the covenant they made with God before entering this world

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r16.claim: Man is an ignorant wrongdoer because he fails to bear the Trust’s full weight.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r16.anchor: Man . . . has proved himself an ignorant wrongdoer insofar as he has failed to bear the full weight of the Trust

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r17.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r17.claim: Some restrict ignorant wrongdoers to disbelievers and hypocrites, who are ignorant of God, and to tyrants.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r17.anchor: some understand this phrase as a reference only to disbelievers and hypocrites, who are ignorant of God

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r18.speaker: M
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r18.claim: Another interpretation refers to Adam, who accepted the Trust without realizing its full import.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r18.anchor: others take it as a reference to Adam, meaning that when he accepted the Trust, he did not realize its full import (M)

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r19.speaker: Ṭū, Z
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r19.claim: Another view applies the phrase to all humans, ignorant of the Trust’s responsibility and wronging themselves through disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r19.anchor: a reference to all human beings who are ignorant of the responsibility of the Trust and wrong themselves by committing acts of disobedience

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r20.speaker: IJ, Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r20.claim: A minority reading takes “bear the Trust” to mean failing to uphold it and thus failing to carry its burden.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r20.anchor: In a minority reading, the expression “bear the Trust” is understood to mean failing to uphold it

STUDYQURAN:33:72/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r21.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r21.claim: One report says Cain bore the Trust’s burden by murdering Abel.
STUDYQURAN:33:72/r21.anchor: it is said that Cain bore the burden of the Trust for having murdered Abel (IJ)

TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r1.claim: One interpretation is that God offered obedience and religious obligations to the heavens, earth, and mountains with reward for fulfilling them and punishment for neglect; they declined from fear of failing, while Adam accepted and was unjust and ignorant of his own interest.
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r1.anchor: أحسنت أثيبت وجوزيت، وإن ضيعت عوقبت، فأبت حملها شفقا منها

TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr identifies the trust as obligations God imposed on servants.
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها} قال: " الأمانة: الفرائض التي افترضها الله على العباد

TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also defines the trust as obligations; a report says Adam accepted them knowing obedience brought forgiveness and disobedience punishment, then sinned later that day.
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها} قال: " الأمانة: الفرائض

TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the heavens, earth, and mountains declined out of reverence for God's religion, not disobedience, fearing they could not fulfill it; Adam accepted it heedlessly.
TAB-FULL:v19p196#3/r4.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال} " إن أدوها أثابهم، وإن ضيعوها عذبهم

TAB-FULL:v19p199/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the trust as obedience: Adam accepted the terms of reward for good and punishment for evil, and Satan led him from the garden between noon and afternoon.
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنا عرضنا الأمانة} [الأحزاب: 72] " الطاعة عرضها عليها قبل أن يعرضها على آدم

TAB-FULL:v19p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says Adam accepted the trust with its conditions and was expelled within a short interval, between noon and afternoon.
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، في قوله: {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} " قال آدم: قيل له: خذها بحقها

TAB-FULL:v19p199/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak calls the trust obedience and dates Adam's expulsion from the garden to a short period after he accepted it.
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال} " فلم يطقن حملها

TAB-FULL:v19p199/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r4.speaker: الحكم بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r4.claim: The Companion Hakam ibn Amr reports the Prophet saying trustworthiness and fidelity descended with Adam's children through the prophets, who taught scripture, religious duties, and distinctions of good and evil; trust was the first quality later lifted, followed by covenants, while scriptures remained.
TAB-FULL:v19p199/r4.anchor: عن الحكم بن عمرو، وكان، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v19p201/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r1.speaker: الحكم بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r1.claim: The prophetic report continues by warning people against the whispering tempter and saying God tests which people do the best deeds.
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r1.anchor: الناس، وإياكم والوسواس الخناس، وإنما يبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا

TAB-FULL:v19p201/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r2.claim: A report says that whoever maintains the five prayers, gives zakat willingly, fasts Ramadan, makes pilgrimage when able, and fulfills the trust enters Paradise; Abu al-Darda identifies this trust as washing after major impurity.
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " خمس من جاء بهن يوم القيامة مع إيمان دخل الجنة

TAB-FULL:v19p201/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says one trust is a woman's responsibility for her sexual chastity.
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: «من الأمانة أن المرأة، اؤتمنت على فرجها»

TAB-FULL:v19p201/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd defines the trust as religious obligations and accountability; the heavens and earth decline, while Adam accepts it and receives help to guard his sight, tongue, and private parts.
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله: {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها} قال: إن الله عرض عليهن الأمانة

TAB-FULL:v19p201/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r5.claim: Qatada says the trust comprises religion, obligations, and limits; creation declines as unable to fulfill it, whereas the human accepts but is unjust and ignorant of its due.
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال} " يعني به: الدين والفرائض والحدود

TAB-FULL:v19p201/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes the trust here to mean people's deposits and other trusts.
TAB-FULL:v19p201/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بالأمانة في هذا الموضع: أمانات الناس

TAB-FULL:v19p202/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r1.claim: A prophetic report says martyrdom erases every sin except a trust: its owner is ordered to return it in the afterlife, finds it at the abyss of Hell, carries it upward, then falls after it forever; trust also includes prayer, fasting, speech, and especially deposits. Al-Bara affirms Ibn Masud's report.
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " القتل في سبيل الله يكفر الذنوب كلها أو قال: يكفر كل شيء إلا الأمانة

TAB-FULL:v19p202/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd transmits Abu Hazim's account that the heavens, earths, and mountains declined the trust, while Adam accepted it and was given counsel to guard his tongue and private parts.
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: أخبرني عمرو بن الحارث، عن ابن أبي هلال، عن أبي حازم

TAB-FULL:v19p202/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the trust as Adam's entrusting Cain with his family, which Cain betrayed by killing his brother Abel.
TAB-FULL:v19p202/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل ذلك إنما عنى به ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل على أهله وولده، وخيانة قابيل أباه في قتله أخاه

TAB-FULL:v19p204/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p204/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p204/r1.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the trust to include every religious duty and people's trusts, since the verse says the trust generally and does not limit it to one kind.
TAB-FULL:v19p204/r1.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ما قاله الذين قالوا: إنه عنى بالأمانة في هذا الموضع

TAB-FULL:v19p204/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p204/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v19p204/r2.claim: Al-Suddi relates the alternative story that Adam asked the heavens, earth, and mountains to guard his children; Cain volunteered, then betrayed the trust by killing Abel after their offerings and marriage dispute.
TAB-FULL:v19p204/r2.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني

TAB-FULL:v19p205/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r1.claim: Al-Suddi applies the description of being unjust and ignorant to Cain, who failed to safeguard Adam's household.
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r1.anchor: عن السدي {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} [الأحزاب: 72] «يعني قابيل حين حمل أمانة آدم لم يحفظ له أهله»

TAB-FULL:v19p205/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the human is Adam, unjust to himself and ignorant about what he undertook before his Lord.
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {وحملها الإنسان} [الأحزاب: 72] " قال آدم {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} [الأحزاب: 72] قال: ظلوما لنفسه

TAB-FULL:v19p205/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Adam's description as being deceived about God's command.
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} [الأحزاب: 72] «غر بأمر الله»

TAB-FULL:v19p205/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r4.claim: Qatada says the human wronged the trust and was ignorant of its due.
TAB-FULL:v19p205/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} [الأحزاب: 72] قال: «ظلوما لها، يعني للأمانة، جهولا عن حقها»

ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr identify the trust as the religious duties God imposed on His servants.
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r1.anchor:
روي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير أنهما قالا: الأمانة ههنا
الفرائض التي افترضها الله على عبادة،

ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says obedience and disobedience, with their reward and punishment, were presented to Adam.
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r2.anchor:
وقال ابن عمر: عرضت على
آدم الطاعة والمعصية وعرف ثواب الطاعة. وعقاب المعصية.

ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r3.claim: The author’s explanation is that God entrusted humans, heaven, earth, and mountains with obedience and submission; revelation says heaven and earth willingly submitted, and other passages describe creation as prostrating or fearing God.
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r3.anchor: وحقيقة هذه الآية - والله أعلم، وهو موافق للتفسير - أن الله عز وجل ائتمن بني آدم على ما افترضه عليهم من طاعته،

ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r4.claim: Heaven, earth, and mountains ‘refused to carry’ the trust by fulfilling it; anyone who betrays a trust or sins is instead said to carry it, as people carry their burdens of sin.
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r4.anchor:
فأعلمنا الله أن السماوات والأرض والجبال لم تحتمل الأمانة، أي
أدتها، وكل من خان الأمانة فقد احتملها،

ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the human who bore the trust but did not obey was the unbeliever and hypocrite; the author endorses this explanation.
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r5.anchor:
وحملها الإنسان، قال الحسن: الكافر والمنافق حملا الأمانة ولم
يطيعا.
فهذا المعنى والله أعلم.

ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r6.claim: The description ‘wrongdoing and ignorant’ does not refer to obedient prophets, the truthful, or believers; the following verse distinguishes punishment for hypocrites and idolaters from repentance for believers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p237#2/r6.anchor:
ومن أطاع من الأنبياء والصديقين والمؤمنين فلا قال كان ظلوما جهولا، وتصديق ذلك ما يتلو هذه الآية
من قوله: (ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات

TABATABAI:33:69-73/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:69-73/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:69-73/r6.claim: An amāna is something entrusted to another to preserve intact and return; here God entrusts humanity with a charge to keep sound and return to Him.
TABATABAI:33:69-73/r6.anchor: الأمانة - أيا ما كانت - شيء يودع عند الغير ليحتفظ عليه ثم يرده إلى من أودعه

TABATABAI:33:69-73/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:69-73/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:69-73/r7.claim: Because carrying or betraying the trust results in hypocrisy, shirk, or faith, the trust must concern true religion.
TABATABAI:33:69-73/r7.anchor: ويستفاد من قوله { ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات } الخ، أنه أمر يترتب على حمله النفاق والشرك والإيمان

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r1.claim: The amāna concerns true religion because taking it up or failing to do so results in hypocrisy, shirk, or faith.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r1.anchor: فهو لا محالة أمر مرتبط بالدين الحق الذي يحصل بالتلبس به وعدم التلبس به النفاق والشرك والإيمان

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r2.claim: It cannot mean bare monotheism: heaven and earth already declare God's unity and praise, while the verse says they refused it.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r2.anchor: وليست هي الأول أعني التوحيد فإن السماوات والأرض وغيرهما من شيء توحده تعالى وتسبح بحمده

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r3.claim: It cannot mean knowing the detailed true religion or acting on it, because every human, including unbelievers who lack its knowledge and observance, is said to bear the trust.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r3.anchor: وليست هي الثاني أعني الدين الحق بتفاصيله فإن الآية تصرح بحمل الإنسان كائنا من كان من مؤمن وغيره له

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r4.claim: It is not the perfection arising from monotheism, since the heavens and earth already exhibit monotheism in action.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r4.anchor: وليست هي الكمال الحاصل له بالتلبس بالتوحيد فإن السماوات والأرض وغيرهما ناطقة بالتوحيد فعلا

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r5.claim: Nor is it perfection from knowing religion: knowledge of beliefs and obligations alone produces neither faith, hypocrisy, shirk, nor happiness and misery; those effects require commitment and practice.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r5.anchor: وليست هي الكمال الحاصل من أخذ دين الحق والعلم به إذ لا يترتب على نفس الاعتقاد الحق والعلم بالتكاليف الدينية نفاق ولا شرك ولا إيمان

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r6.claim: The amāna is divine guardianship: perfection attained by belief, righteous action, and ascent from materiality to exclusive sincerity, where God takes charge of the person's affairs.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r6.anchor: فبقي أنها الكمال الحاصل له من جهة التلبس بالاعتقاد والعمل الصالح وسلوك سبيل الكمال بالارتقاء من حضيض المادة إلى أوج الإخلاص

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r7.claim: Offering the trust means considering whether these creations could bear it; carrying or refusing means having or lacking readiness. Vast heaven, earth, and mountains lack that potential, while humankind accepted it.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r7.anchor: والمراد بحملها والإباء عنه وجود استعدادها وصلاحية التلبس بها وعدمه، وهذا المعنى هو القابل لأن ينطبق على الآية

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r8.claim: The human's reckless acceptance leads to division into hypocrites, polytheists, and believers according to whether the trust is preserved or betrayed; creation beyond humanity remains obedient.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r8.anchor: فتعقب ذلك أن انقسم الإنسان من جهة حفظ الأمانة وعدمه بالخيانة إلى منافق ومشرك ومؤمن

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r9.claim: The objection is that entrusting a weak, unjust, ignorant human with a burden the mighty heavens refused resembles appointing a madman to a public office that wise people avoid.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r9.anchor: فإن قلت ما بال الحكيم العليم حمل على هذا المخلوق الظلوم الجهول حملا لا يتحمله لثقله وعظم خطره

TABATABAI:33:63-73/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī answers that injustice and ignorance qualify humans for the trust because only a being capable of justice and knowledge can also fail at them; mountains and worlds cannot be so described.
TABATABAI:33:63-73/r10.anchor: قلت الظلم والجهل في الإنسان وإن كانا بوجه ملاك اللوم والعتاب فهما بعينهما مصحح حمله الأمانة والولاية الإلهية

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r1.claim: The trust is divine guardianship and complete servanthood, attained through knowing God and righteous action, which is justice.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r1.anchor: والأمانة المذكورة في الآية وهي الولاية الإلهية وكمال صفة العبودية إنما تتحصل بالعلم بالله والعمل الصالح الذي هو العدل

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r2.claim: Human receptivity to the trust rests on being capable by nature of ignorance and injustice, and thus able to receive knowledge and justice and rise beyond them.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r2.anchor: فكون الإنسان في حد نفسه وبحسب طبعه ظلوما جهولا هو المصحح لحمل الأمانة الإلهية فافهم ذلك

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r3.claim: The trust passage resembles the account of humanity made excellent and then fallen, except for those who believe and do good.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r3.anchor: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r4.claim: Offering the trust means considering divine guardianship and religious completion in relation to the heavens, earth, and mountains.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r4.anchor: أي الولاية الإلهية والاستكمال بحقائق الدين الحق علما وعملا وعرضها هو اعتبارها مقيسة إلى هذه الأشياء

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r5.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains are immense creatures, greater in creation than people.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r5.anchor: هذه المخلوقات العظيمة التي خلقها أعظم من خلق الإنسان كما قال

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r6.claim: Their refusal and fear mean they lacked fitness to take on the trust and recoiled from accepting it; the image of carrying signals its unbearable weight.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r6.anchor: إباؤها عن حملها وإشفاقها منها عدم اشتمالها على صلاحية التلبس وتجافيها عن قبولها وفي التعبير بالحمل إيماء إلى أنها ثقيلة ثقلا

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r7.claim: Humanity carried it by having the capacity and readiness to take it on despite its weakness and small size.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r7.anchor: أي اشتمل على صلاحيتها والتهيؤ للتلبس بها على ضعفه وصغر حجمه

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r8.claim: The human is unjust to himself and ignorant of the dire, lasting ruin that betrayal of the trust brings.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r8.anchor: أي ظالما لنفسه جاهلا بما تعقبه هذه الأمانة لو خانها من وخيم العاقبة والهلاك الدائم

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r9.claim: More precisely, humans begin without justice or knowledge but can receive them and rise from injustice and ignorance to their heights.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r9.anchor: بحسب نفسه عن العدل والعلم قابلا للتلبس بما يفاض عليه من ذلك والارتقاء من حضيض الظلم والجهل إلى أوج العدل

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r10.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r10.claim: The intensive adjectives ظلوم and جهول can mean that injustice and ignorance are characteristic dispositions.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r10.anchor: شأنها ذلك كما قاله الرازي أو معناهما المبالغة في الظلم والجهل كما

TABATABAI:33:72-73/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r11.speaker: غيره
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r11.claim: Another view takes ظلوم and جهول as intensives meaning extreme injustice and ignorance; either interpretation fits.
TABATABAI:33:72-73/r11.anchor: أو معناهما المبالغة في الظلم والجهل كما ذكر غيره، والمعنى مستقيم كيفما كانا.

TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r7.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r7.claim: A passage in Nahj al-Balagha depicts the immense heavens, earth, and mountains refusing the trust through fear of punishment, while weaker humanity was ignorant of what they understood.
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r7.anchor: فلا أطول ولا أعرض ولا أعلى ولا أعظم منها ولو امتنع شيء بطول أو عرض أو قوة أو عز لامتنعن ولكن أشفقن من العقوبة

TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r8.claim: A report in al-Kafi identifies the trust as the wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful.
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r8.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن إسحاق بن عمار عن رجل عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل

TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r9.claim: The wilayah report applies the trust to Ali as the first in the community to open this path: God's taking charge of a person through sincere servanthood, rather than love or imamate as such.
TABATABAI:33:63-73#2/r9.anchor: ما كان هو أول فاتح لبابه من هذه الأمة وهو كون الإنسان، بحيث يتولى الله سبحانه أمره بمجاهدته فيه بإخلاص

TABRISI:33:70-72/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
TABRISI:33:70-72/r7.claim: One view defines the trust as everything God commands people to obey and forbids them to violate.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r7.anchor: هي ما أمر الله به من طاعته ونهى عنه من معصيته عن أبي العالية

TABRISI:33:70-72/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:33:70-72/r8.claim: Another view defines the trust as God's legal rulings and obligations; the author says it is close to the first view.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r8.anchor: هي الأحكام والفرائض التي أوجبها الله تعالى على العباد عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وهذان القولان متقاربان

TABRISI:33:70-72/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r9.speaker: السدي والضحاك
TABRISI:33:70-72/r9.claim: A further view means people's trusts and keeping covenants; it begins with Adam entrusting his family to Cain before traveling to Mecca, after which Cain betrayed him by killing Abel.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r9.anchor: هي أمانات الناس والوفاء بالعهود فأولها ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل على أهله وولده

TABRISI:33:70-72/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:70-72/r10.claim: One explanation takes the presentation as addressed to the inhabitants of heavens, earth, and mountains, with a deleted possessive; they were shown the grave sin of violating God's trusts and laws, displaying human boldness and the angels' fear.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r10.anchor: المراد العرض على أهلها فحذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

TABRISI:33:70-72/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r11.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:33:70-72/r11.claim: The inhabitants refused the liability, sin, and punishment for neglecting the trust, and feared it; humankind carried it by sinning, ignorant of the consequences of betrayal.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r11.anchor: أي فأبى أهلهن أن يحملوا تركها وعقابها والمأثم فيها { وأشفقن منها } أي

TABRISI:33:70-72/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r12.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:33:70-72/r12.claim: Because the physical heavens, earth, and mountains cannot bear moral responsibility, the verse must mean their accountable inhabitants; bearing the trust means violating it, since angels already perform it.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r12.anchor: إذا لم يصح حمله على نفس السماوات والأرض والجبال فلا بد أن يكون المراد به أهلها

TABRISI:33:70-72/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:70-72/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:33:70-72/r13.claim: Zajjaj says a betrayer bears the trust while one who fulfills it has not; likewise, sinners bear the burden of sin.
TABRISI:33:70-72/r13.anchor: كل من خان الأمانة فقد حملها ومن لم يحمل الأمانة فقد أداها

TABRISI:33:72/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:33:72/r1.claim: Al-Hasan understands carrying the trust as betraying it; the author says the apparent sense does not support this reading.
TABRISI:33:72/r1.anchor: لأنه قال: الكافر والمنافق حملا الأمانة أي خانا ولم يطيعا

TABRISI:33:72/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:72/r2.claim: The poet's usage makes accepting a trust the opposite of returning it, so it cannot show that carrying here means betrayal.
TABRISI:33:72/r2.anchor: إذا كنت لا تزال تقبل أمانة وتؤدي أخرى شغلت نفسك بقبول الودائع

TABRISI:33:72/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:33:72/r3.claim: The offer means comparison: God's trust comprises commands, prohibitions, books, messengers, and the covenant, outweighing the heavens, earth, and mountains in importance.
TABRISI:33:72/r3.anchor: والأمانة ما عهد الله سبحانه إلى عباده من أمره ونهيه وأنزل فيه الكتب

TABRISI:33:72/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:33:72/r4.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains could not bear the trust and feared it; the human accepted but neglected it through injustice and ignorance of reward and punishment.
TABRISI:33:72/r4.anchor: تقلدها الإنسان فلم يحفظها بل حملها وضيعها لظلمه على نفسه

TABRISI:33:72/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:72/r5.claim: Hypothetically, if the heavens, earth, and mountains were rational, they would fear failing the religious duties and promises or threats; a weaker human accepted without fear.
TABRISI:33:72/r5.anchor: لو كانت السموات والأرض والجبال عاقلة ثم عرضت عليها الأمانة وهي وظائف الدين

TABRISI:33:72/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:33:72/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's report that the trust was offered to the actual heavens and earth is understood on this hypothetical reading.
TABRISI:33:72/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا يحمل ما روي عن ابن عباس أنها عرضت على نفس السموات والأرض

TABRISI:33:72/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:72/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:33:72/r7.claim: Alternatively, offer and refusal figuratively exalt the trust rather than describe speech to inanimate things; Arabs similarly address ruins and houses as if they could answer.
TABRISI:33:72/r7.anchor: بل المراد تعظيم شأن الأمانة لا مخاطبة الجماد والعرب تقول سألت الربع وخاطبت الدار

THALABI:v8p67/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p67/r1.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains refused the trust out of reverent fear, not disobedience; its offer was a choice, not a compulsion.
THALABI:v8p67/r1.anchor: فأبين أن يحملنها مخافة وخشية لا معصية ومخالفة، وكان العرض تخييرا لا إلزاما

THALABI:v8p67/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v8p67/r2.claim: Most commentators say the trust is obedience and the obligatory duties: performance earns reward and neglect incurs punishment.
THALABI:v8p67/r2.anchor: فقال أكثر المفسرين: هي الطاعة والفرائض التي فرضها الله على عباده

THALABI:v8p67/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p67/r3.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains declined because they revered God's religion and did not want reward or punishment; they said they were already subjected to His command.
THALABI:v8p67/r3.anchor: فكرهوا ذلك وأشفقوا من غير معصية، ولكن تعظيما لدين الله أن لا يقوموا بها

THALABI:v8p67/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p67/r4.claim: God offered Adam the trust with its consequences; Adam accepted it, and God promised help by giving him guards over sight, speech, and sexual exposure.
THALABI:v8p67/r4.anchor: إني عرضت الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فلم يطقنها، فهل أنت آخذها بما فيها؟

THALABI:v8p67/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p67/r5.claim: The report says Adam remained in Paradise only from noon until afternoon before being sent out.
THALABI:v8p67/r5.anchor: قالوا: فما لبث آدم إلا مقدارا ما بين الظهر والعصر حتى أخرج من الجنة

THALABI:v8p67/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p67/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the trust as religious obligations and boundaries.
THALABI:v8p67/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الأمانة الفرائض وحدود الدين

THALABI:v8p67/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v8p67/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the trust consists of what people were commanded and forbidden to do.
THALABI:v8p67/r7.anchor: وأبو العالية: هي ما أمروا به ونهوا عنه

THALABI:v8p67/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم وغيره
THALABI:v8p67/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and others identify the trust as fasting, ritual bathing after intercourse, and hidden religious rules.
THALABI:v8p67/r8.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم وغيره: هي الصوم والغسل من الجنابة وما يخفى من شرائع الدين

THALABI:v8p67/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r9.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v8p67/r9.claim: Abu Darda says five deeds together with faith lead to Paradise: keeping the prayers in their proper form and times, paying zakat willingly, and fulfilling the trust.
THALABI:v8p67/r9.anchor: خمس من جاء بهن يوم القيامة مع إيمان دخل الجنة: من حافظ على الصلوات

THALABI:v8p67/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p67/r10.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v8p67/r10.claim: Asked what fulfilling the trust means, Abu Darda says it is washing after ritual impurity; God entrusted no other part of religion to people in this way.
THALABI:v8p67/r10.anchor: قالوا: يا أبا الدرداء، وما أداء الأمانة؟ قال: الغسل من الجنابة

ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n87/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n87/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n87/r1.claim: Although classical commentators give many explanations of amanah, Asad finds the most convincing readings to be reason or intellect and the faculty of volition, the ability to choose good or evil.
ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n87/r1.anchor: the most convincing of them (mentioned in Lane 1, 102, with reference to the above verse) are "reason", or "intellect", and "the faculty of volition"

ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n88/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n88/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n88/r1.claim: Zamakhshari explains that humanity took up reason and relative free will but failed to meet the moral responsibility they entail; this describes the human race, not necessarily every individual.
ASAD-NOTES:33:72#n88/r1.anchor: failed to measure up to the moral responsibility arising from the reason and the comparative free will with which he has been endowed" (Zamakhshari)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the trust is the duties God imposed on people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r1.anchor: الأمانة الفرائض التي افترضها الله على العباد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the trust with religion as a whole.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r2.anchor: الحسن: هو الدين، فالدين كله أمانة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the trust includes all that people are commanded to do and forbidden to do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r3.anchor: الأمانة ما أمروا به وما نهوا عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r5.claim: The interpreters’ definitions converge on obedience and duties whose performance earns reward and whose neglect incurs punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r5.anchor: والأمانة في هذه الآية في قول جميعهم: الطاعة والفرائض التي (¬8) يتعلق بأدائها الثواب وبتضييعها العقاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam transmits a report from the Prophet that names prayer, fasting, and ritual washing after major impurity as the three trusts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r6.anchor: زيد بن أسلم عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أنه قال: "الأمانة ثلاثة: الصلاة # والصيام والغسل من الجنابة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes the seven heavens, earths, and mountains being offered the trust with its reward and punishment; they refuse, and the verse says they declined and feared it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r7.anchor: الحسن في هذه الآية قال: عرضت الأمانة على السموات السبع الطباق التي زينت بالنجوم وحملت العرش العظيم، فقيل لهن: أتأخذن الأمانة بما فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports the heavens saying they were created as a protected roof and cannot carry a duty or seek reward or punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r8.anchor: ابن جريج: قالت السموات: يا رب خلقتني وجعلتني سقفا محفوظا، وأجريت في الشمس والقمر، لا أتحمل فريضة ولا أبتغي ثوابا ولا عقابا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r9.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says the heavens, earth, and mountains accepted obedience to God but said they lacked strength to accept this trust with its reward and punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r9.anchor: يا رب إنا لا نستطيع هذا الأمر وليست بنا قوة ولكنا لك مطيعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r10.claim: He accepts the direct account that the offer was made to these entities themselves, with God giving them understanding and speech; their refusal was fear, not disobedience, and the offer was a choice rather than a binding imposition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r10.anchor: ركب الله تعالى فيهن العقول ويفهمن (¬2) خطابهن حتى فهمن ونطقن بالجواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r11.claim: Their refusal came from fear and apprehension, not disobedience, and the offer was an option rather than a compulsory demand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p302#2/r11.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {فأبين أن يحملنها} أي: مخافة وخشية، لا معصية ومخالفة، والعرض كان تخييرا لا لزاما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts God offering Adam the trust with its reward and punishment; Adam agreed and was expelled from Paradise after only the interval between the first prayer and afternoon, through Satan’s action.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: قال الله لآدم: إني عرضت الأمانة على السموات والأرض فلم تطقها أفتحملها أنت [بما فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s report, the trust given to Adam comprises the obligatory prayers at their times, zakāt, Ramadan fasting, and pilgrimage, with reward and punishment attached; Adam accepts it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r2.anchor: عطاء: {وحملها الإنسان} يريد آدم -عليه السلام-، عرض عليه أداء الفرائض والصلوات الخمس في مواقيتها، وأداء الزكاة عند محلها، وصام رمضان وحج البيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r3.speaker: ابن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r3.claim: Ibn Ḥayyān gives another dialogue: Adam asks what he receives, learns of honor and Paradise for obedience and punishment for disobedience, and accepts the trust.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r3.anchor: فقال آدم: وما لي عندك؟ قال: إن أحسنت وأطعت ورعيت الأمانة فذلك الكرامة وحسن الثواب في الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r4.speaker: ابن عثمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUthmān says Adam was shown obedience and disobedience and learned their respective reward and punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r4.anchor: عرضت على آدم الطاعة والمعصية وعرف ثواب الطاعة وعقاب المعصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī says Adam was unjust when he disobeyed and was expelled, and ignorant when he undertook the trust.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r5.anchor: ظلمه حين عصى ربه فأخرج من الجنة وجهله حين احتملها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r6.speaker: المقاتلان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r6.claim: The two Muqātils interpret Adam as unjust to himself and ignorant of the outcome of what he undertook.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r6.anchor: ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بعاقبة ما تحمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r7.claim: Qatāda says Adam wronged the trust and was ignorant of its due.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r8.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r8.claim: Al-Suddī offers an alternative story: Adam entrusted Cain with his family while he went to the House in Mecca, and Cain accepted but killed Abel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r8.anchor: الأمانة هي ائتمان آدم ابنه قابيل على أهله وولده وخيانته إياه في قتل أخيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r9.claim: Abū Isḥāq says God entrusted Adam’s descendants with His prescribed obedience, while the heavens, earth, and mountains fulfilled their trust by obeying; those who sin are said to bear the trust as they bear sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r9.anchor: أبو إسحاق: حقيقة تفسير هذه الآية -والله أعلم- أن الله تعالى ائتمن بني آدم على ما افترض عليهم من طاعته، وائتمن السموات والأرض والجبال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r10.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the human who bore and betrayed the trust to be the unbeliever and hypocrite; the obedient are not called unjust and ignorant, as the next verse confirms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p304/r10.anchor: الحسن: أراد الكافر والمنافق حملا الأمانة أي: خانا ولم يطيعا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r1.claim: The trust is God’s prescribed obligations, whose fulfillment earns reward and betrayal punishment; God made the heavens, earth, and mountains understand and speak, but they declined from fear, not disobedience.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r2.claim: Adam accepted the trust, thereby wronging himself and being naïve about God’s command and the burden assumed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:72-73/r2.anchor: غرا بأمر الله سبحانه وما احتمل من الأمانة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r2.claim: The trust offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains comprised reward and punishment, obedience and disobedience.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says worship was offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains with its rewards and punishments; they refused it, while Adam accepted.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r3.anchor: عرض العبادة على السموات، والأرض، والجبال

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the human’s trust as prayer, fasting, and washing after major impurity.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says God entrusted Adam with prayer, fasting, and washing after major impurity; keeping them makes one God’s servant, neglecting them His enemy, and one could falsely claim to have done them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r5.anchor: ثلاث من حفظهن فهو عبدي حقا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p741#2/r6.claim: Adam, the human bearer, was unjust to himself.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p742/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p742/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p742/r1.claim: “Ignorant” means ignorant of his Lord, describing the polytheist.

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r1.claim: Amāna derives as a verbal noun from the root of security and trustworthiness, and came also to name what is entrusted; it is broader than a deposit, with the first sense fitting this verse better.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r1.anchor: “Emânet” aslında “mîm”in zammıyla أمن يأمن’den masdar olup eminlik, yani âharın hukūku emniyet edilip inanılabilir

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r2.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r2.claim: Most exegetes interpret the trust as religious obligations or duties.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r2.anchor: Ekseriyetle müfessirîn bunu teklif veya ferâiz

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r3.claim: The trust is voluntary vicegerency: carrying out God's commands and prohibitions concerning His and people's rights, unlike the compelled obedience of other things.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r3.anchor: Allah’ın gerek kendi hukūkuna ve gerek halkın hukūkuna müte‘allik emr ü nehyinin, ahkâmının icrâsına Allah’ın emîni

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r4.claim: The heavens and earth accepted God's creational command willingly, as in 41:11, but balked when asked to carry the trust concerning others' rights.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r4.anchor: öyle iken âharın hukūkunu yüklenmek mânasını ifade eden emanet kendilerine arz olunduğu zaman çekindiler

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r5.speaker: müfessirler
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r5.claim: Some exegetes take the offer and refusal literally; many instead see a representative metaphor picturing the trust's immense weight.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r5.anchor: çokları emânetin azametini beyan için isti‘âre-i temsîliye suretinde bir tasvir olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r6.claim: Fulfilling the trust brings great honor, while failing to fulfill it brings betrayal, liability, and disgrace.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r6.anchor: Emânet îfâ edildiği takdirde neticesi çok büyük bir keramet olduğu gibi, îfâ edilemediği takdirde de hıyânet ve garâmetle büyük bir rüsvâlıktır

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r7.claim: Humanity accepted the trust and vicegerency, but "very unjust, very ignorant" describes the human kind rather than every individual.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r7.anchor: O insan cidden zalûm cehûl bulunuyor her ferdi değil, insan cinsi

ELMALILI:33:72-73/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r8.claim: The human is unjust by neglecting God's and other people's rights and thereby wronging himself; ignorant because he does not grasp the outcome of his choice.
ELMALILI:33:72-73/r8.anchor: Allah’ın ve ibâdullahın hukūkunu yüklendiği hâlde lâyıkıyla îfâ etmeyip kendine yazık ediyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r1.claim: The verse uses simile and parable; the author's preferred reading is figurative: the trust is too weighty for seemingly stronger heavens, earth, and mountains, yet humans undertook it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r1.anchor: bizim tercihimiz burada bir temsilî anlatımın söz konusu olduğudur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r2.speaker: bazı tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r2.claim: A literal reading says God gave the heavens, earth, and mountains consciousness in eternity, offered them the trust, and they refused before the ignorant, poorly judging human accepted it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r2.anchor: Allah’ın ezelde, göklere, yere ve dağlara şuur verdiğini, emaneti almayı onlara teklif ettiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r3.claim: Humans have the capacity to carry the trust but may not understand it or fulfill it; they must recognize their identity, abilities, and duty, since ignorance is folly and neglect is injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r3.anchor: o, bir yandan bunu yüklenecek kabiliyet ve yetenektedir, ama öte yandan neyi yüklendiğinin farkında değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r4.claim: Lexically, amana means the removal of fear and anxiety and secure confidence; it can name either this state or the thing entrusted for protection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r4.anchor: Emanet kelimesinin sözlük anlamı “korku ve kaygının gitmesi, insanın korunma konusunda gönül rahatlığı içinde olması”dır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r5.claim: The closest religious senses are tawhid and its belief, justice, literacy, reason, capacity for moral responsibility, and trust in the Turkish sense; these gather under reason- and free-will-based obligation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r5.anchor: “tevhid kelimesi ve inancı, adalet, okuma-yazma, akıl ve yükümlü (mükellef) olma kabiliyeti ve Türkçe’deki anlamıyla emanet”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r6.claim: Other creatures follow their created programming, whereas humans can learn and change decisions and actions but face serious barriers to recognizing and doing good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r6.anchor: onda akıl, bilgi edinme, bilgisini, kararını ve davranışını değiştirme kabiliyeti vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r7.claim: Without divine knowledge and guidance, humans know far less than they do not know and fail more often at moral good, explaining the verse's descriptions as extremely ignorant and unjust.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r7.anchor: (72. âyetteki deyimiyle insan cehûldür, çok bilgisizdir); din ve ahlâk konusunda kötülükleri iyiliklerinden çoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r8.claim: The entrusted capacity for obligation can make a person the noblest creature if honored, but misusing it under Satan's influence brings the person to the lowest level.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r8.anchor: eşref-i mahlûkat (yaratılmışların en değerlisi ve şereflisi) olur; hakkını veremezse

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r9.claim: If amana is taken in its ordinary Turkish sense, the verse highlights material possessions and spiritual duties as important examples within broader obligations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:72/r9.anchor: daha genel olan yükümlülükler kümesi içinden bir önemlisi öne çıkarılmış olur

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada identify the trust offered to the heavens, earth, and mountains as God’s religious obligations, which those creations refused to bear.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r1.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله ﴿ إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r2.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the trust is God’s obligations; the heavens, earth, and mountains could not bear them, so Adam accepted after being told he would be rewarded for good and punished for evil.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال ﴾ قال هي فرائض قال وقوله ﴿ فأبين أن يحملنها ﴾ قال فلم تستطعها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports from the Prophet that the trust consists of prayer, fasting, and washing after major ritual impurity.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الأمانة ثلاث الصلاة والصيام والغسل من الجنابة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka‘b says that one form of the trust is a woman being entrusted with guarding her chastity.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r4.anchor: عن مسلم أبي الضحى عن مسروق عن أبي بن كعب قال من الأمانة أن المرأة أؤتمنت على فرجها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r5.speaker: وهب الديناري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r5.claim: Wahb al-Dinari cites a statement written in the Psalms: whoever performs the ritual bath after major impurity is truly God’s servant, while whoever neglects it is His enemy.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p125/r5.anchor: قال أخبرني وهب الديناري قال في الزبور مكتوب أن الله يقول من اغتسل من الجنابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r1.claim: The trust most likely encompasses every charge entrusted to people, including commands and prohibitions and religious and worldly duties; the whole revealed law is a trust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r1.anchor: والأمانة: الظاهر أنها كل ما يؤتمن عليه من أمر ونهي وشأن دين ودنيا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka‘b gives the example of a woman being entrusted with guarding her sexual chastity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال أبي زين كعب: من الأمانة أن اؤتمنت المرأة على فرجها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda considers washing after major ritual impurity a trust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: غسل الجنابة أمانة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r4.claim: The offer to the immense created bodies and their refusal and fear can be literal, since God may grant created things perception, as in other miracles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r4.anchor: وهذا غير مستحيل، إذ قد سبح الحصى في كفه عليه الصلاة والسلام، وحن الجذع إليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says inanimate things were given understanding and discrimination and offered a choice about carrying the trust; mountains are singled out to emphasize the burden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أعطيت الجمادات فهما وتمييزا، فخيرت في الحمل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the offer was audible to Adam and the refusal audible from inanimate things, demonstrating the trust and Adam’s zeal and distinction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: عرضت بمسمع من آدم، عليه الصلاة والسلام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r7.claim: Other interpretations treat the passage figuratively, either by ellipsis for the beings in the heavens and earth or as personification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو مجاز، فقيل: من مجاز الحذف، أي على من فيها من الملائكة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r8.claim: Zamakhshari reads the scene as an imagined comparison that dramatizes how weighty human obligations would be even for the mightiest created bodies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أن ما كلفه الإنسان بلغ من عظمه وثقل محمله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r9.claim: Zamakhshari compares the figurative speech to Arabic sayings that make fat or animals speak, though the imagined speech is impossible in fact.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509/r9.anchor: من ذلك قول العرب: لو قيل للشحم أين تذهب لقيل: أسوي العوج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r1.claim: Zamakhshari answers that the comparison is mentally posited as a hypothetical, so an impossible imagined scene can illustrate the real weight of obligation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r1.anchor: الممثل به في الآية، وفي قولهم: لو قيل للشحم أين تذهب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r2.claim: He also argues that inanimate bodies submit to God in ways appropriate to them, while humans are capable of obeying commands and prohibitions but fail to do so.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r2.anchor: هذه الأجرام العظام قد انقادت لأمر الله انقياد مثلها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r3.claim: On this allegorical reading, the trust means obedience; the heavens and earth decline it figuratively, while humans accept it and fail to discharge it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالأمانة: الطاعة، لأنها لازمة للوجود. كما أن الأمانة لازمة للأداء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r4.claim: “Carrying” an obligation is a metaphor based on the trust riding on its custodian until performance clears the debt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r4.anchor: وحمل الأمانة من قولك: فلان حامل للأمانة ومحتمل لها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r5.claim: The human is called unjust for failing to discharge the trust and ignorant for missing the benefit of fulfilling it despite being able.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r5.anchor: ثم وصفه بالظلم لكونه تاركا لأداء الأمانة، وبالجهل لخطئه ما يسعده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p509#2/r6.claim: Zamakhshari’s allegorical explanation contains an omitted element, as the author notes.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r1.claim: Another figurative reading compares the trust’s weight with the strength of the heavens, earth, and mountains: they would fall short and refuse if they could speak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r1.anchor: وقال قوم: الآية من المجاز، أي إذا قايسنا ثقل الأمانة بقوة السموات والأرض والجبال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r2.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r2.claim: Ibn Bahr explains “عرضنا” as comparing the trust with the created bodies, and “أبين” as being unable to bear it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r2.anchor: ونحوه قول ابن بحر» معنى عرضنا: عارضناها وقابلناها بها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr say the human accepted responsibility for the trust’s duties; the human is Adam, unjust to himself and ignorant of the burden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وابن جبير: التزم القيام بحقها، والإنسان آدم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam did not last even a day before being expelled from Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما تم له يوم حتى أخرج من الجنة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r5.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan interpret carrying the trust as betraying it; the human refers to unbelievers, hypocrites, and sinners in differing degrees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك، والحسن: وحملها معناه: خان فيها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r6.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud and another report from Ibn Abbas identify the human with Cain, who had promised Adam to protect the family while Adam was away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r6.anchor: وكان قد تحمل لأبيه أمانة أن يحفظ الأهل بعده،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets the trust as signs of divine oneness in created things and carrying it as betrayal or taking it away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r7.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: عرض الأمانة: وضع شواهد الوحدانية في المصنوعات:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r8.claim: The author says Ibn Ishaq’s cited poem does not prove that “carrying” means taking something away; it can mean continually assuming further trusts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p510/r8.anchor: وليس وتحمل أخرى نصا في الذهاب بها،

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r1.claim: After describing punishment for disobedience and reward for obedience to God and the Messenger, the passage magnifies the weight and difficulty of religious duties by parable, while indicating acceptance and refusal were voluntary.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r1.anchor: عظم شأن ما يوجبها من التكاليف الشرعية وصعوبة أمرها بطريق التمثيل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r2.claim: Amanah, a verbal noun related to security and trust, depicts duties as rights God entrusted to accountable beings, requiring willing obedience, careful preservation, and complete delivery.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r2.anchor: وهي في الأصل مصدر كالأمن والأمان تنبيها على أنها حقوق مرعية أودعها الله تعالى المكلفين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r3.claim: Calling the duty an offer to the heavens, earth, and mountains represents assessing their particular capacities and stresses solicitude and desire for their acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r3.anchor: وعبر عن اعتبارها بالنسبة إلى استعداد ما ذكر من السموات وغيرها من حيث الخصوصيات بالعرض عليهن

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r4.claim: Their refusal and fear represent their incapacity and the duty's incompatibility with their nature, heightening its gravity; carrying it represents its heaviness.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r4.anchor: وعن عدم استعدادهن لقبولها ومنافاتها لما هن عليه بالإباء والإشفاق منها لتهويل أمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r5.claim: The counterfactual means that if these mighty bodies had consciousness and were charged with the trust, they would refuse and fear it; the wording presents the supposition as fact to make the point vivid.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r5.anchor: لو كلفت هاتيك الأجرام العظام التي هي مثل في القوة والشدة مراعاتها وكانت ذات شعور وإدراك لأبين قبولها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r6.claim: “The human” means the human species, as in the verses describing humanity as ungrateful and transgressive; bearing the trust means readiness to accept it or undertaking it at the primordial covenant despite frailty.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r6.anchor: وحملها الإنسان ( أي هذا الجنس نحو ( إن الإنسان لربه لكنود

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r7.claim: Humanity may have accepted through its innate capacity or through a spoken pledge on the day of the covenant; humans are singled out although jinn are also accountable, since angels face no hardship contrary to their nature.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r7.anchor: بتكليفه إياها يوم الميثاق أي تكلفها والتزمها مع ما فيه من ضعف البنية ورخاوة القوة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r8.claim: The statement that humanity is unjust and ignorant interrupts the account to foreshadow failure and answer possible doubt; it describes the majority who violate their original nature or pledge, not those who preserve God's nature-given disposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p96/r8.anchor: اعتراض وسط بين الحمل وغايته للإيذان من أول الأمر بعدم وفائه بما تحمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the trust is obedience and the religious duties God imposed, offered with reward for fulfilling them and punishment for neglecting them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r1.anchor: عرضها على السموات والأرض والجبال على أنهم إن أدوها أثابهم وإن ضيعوها عذبهم، وهذا قول ابن عباس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r2.claim: Ibn Masud lists the trust as prayer, zakat, Ramadan fasting, pilgrimage, truthful speech, repaying debt, justice in measure and weight, and especially entrusted deposits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r2.anchor: ابن مسعود: الأمانة: أداء الصلوات، وإيتاء الزكاة، وصوم رمضان، وحج البيت، وصدق الحديث، وقضاء الدين، والعدل في المكيال والميزان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r3.claim: Mujahid says the trust means duties and repaying debts.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya says it is what people are commanded and forbidden to do.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r4.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: ما أمروا به ونهوا عنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies it as fasting, washing after sexual impurity, and hidden religious laws.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r5.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: هو الصوم، والغسل من الجنابة، وما يخفى من الشرائع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r6.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says bodily faculties, beginning with sexual organs, are trusts from God; one who lacks trustworthiness lacks faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أول ما خلق الله من الإنسان فرجه وقال: هذه أمانة استودعتكها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r7.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r7.claim: Another view, transmitted by al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas, defines the trust as people's trusts and keeping covenants, forbidding betrayal of believers or protected non-Muslims in any matter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r7.anchor: وهي رواية الضحاك عن ابن عباس، فعرض الله هذه الأمانة على أعيان السموات والأرض والجبال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and many early authorities say the offer was made to the actual heavens, earth, and mountains, who declined out of awe and fear of failing the trust, not rebellion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r8.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس وجماعة من التابعين وأكثر السلف، فقال لهن أتحملن هذه الأمانة بما فيها؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r9.claim: The offer was a choice, not an obligation; had they been compelled, they would not have refused. All created things submit to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r9.anchor: وكان العرض عليهن تخييرا لا إلزاما ولو ألزمهن لم يمتنعن من حملها، والجمادات كلها خاضعة لله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r10.claim: The passage's submission of creation is linked to God's command to heaven and earth and reports of stones and creatures bowing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380/r10.anchor: كما قال جل ذكره للسموات والأرض: "ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r1.claim: Some scholars say God gave the heavens, earth, and mountains understanding when He offered the trust, so they understood and answered.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم: ركب الله عز وجل فيهن العقل والفهم حين عرض الأمانة عليهن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r2.claim: Some say the offer was addressed to the inhabitants of the heavens and earth, namely the angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: المراد من العرض على السموات والأرض هو العرض على أهل السموات والأرض،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r3.claim: Another view takes the offer as directed to the inhabitants only, like asking a town means asking its people; Baghawi says the first view, addressing the entities themselves, is sounder.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: على أهلها كلها دون أعيانها، كقوله تعالى: "واسئل القرية"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r4.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains feared failing the trust and being punished; Adam accepted after being told that good brings reward and evil punishment, and God promised practical help to guard sight, speech, and chastity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r4.anchor: {فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها} أي: خفن من الأمانة أن لا يؤدينها فيلحقهن العقاب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says only the span between noon and afternoon passed between Adam accepting the trust and leaving the Garden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: فما كان بين أن تحملها وبين أن خرج من الجنة إلا مقدار ما بين الظهر والعصر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r6.claim: A report ascribed to Ibn Masud by al-Naqqash compares the trust to a stone: the heavens, earth, and mountains declined, but Adam volunteered, carried it to his shoulder after successive trials, and God declared it a burden on him and his descendants until Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r6.anchor: وحكى النقاش بإسناده عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: مثلت الأمانة كصخرة ملقاة، ودعيت السموات والأرض والجبال إليها فلم يقربوا منها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Adam as wronging himself and ignorant of God's command and the trust he undertook.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p380#2/r7.anchor: {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} قال ابن عباس: ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بأمر الله وما احتمل من الأمانة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says Adam was unjust when he disobeyed God and ignorant of the punishment for neglecting the trust.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r1.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ظلوما حين عصى ربه، جهولا لا يدري ما العقاب في ترك الأمانة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r2.claim: Muqatil says Adam wronged himself and did not know the consequences of what he accepted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بعاقبة ما تحمل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj and other language scholars offer two interpretations: humans bear duties and creation bears submission; or creation fulfilled its trust while the human bore it by betraying it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r3.anchor: وذكر الزجاج وغيره من أهل المعاني، في قوله وحملها الإنسان قولان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r4.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r4.claim: On the betrayal interpretation, Hasan says the human who bore the trust means a disbeliever or hypocrite who betrayed it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r4.anchor: حكي عن الحسن على هذا التأويل: أنه قال وحملها الإنسان يعني الكافر والمنافق، حملا الأمانة أي: خانا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p381/r5.claim: Baghawī endorses the early authorities' interpretation of the trust as obedience and duties described above.

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r5.claim: The trust is named amāna because its performance is obligatory; this reinforces the preceding promise by magnifying obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r5.anchor: تقرير للوعد السابق بتعظيم الطاعة، وسماها أمانة من حيث إنها واجبة الأداء

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r6.claim: The offer to immense celestial bodies is a hypothetical emphasizing the trust's gravity: if conscious, they would refuse and fear it, while frail humans carried it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r6.anchor: لو عرضت على هذه الأجرام العظام وكانت ذات شعور وإدراك لأبين أن يحملنها

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r7.claim: Safeguarding the trust and fulfilling its rights brings good in both abodes; people are generally unjust for failing it and ignorant of its consequences.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r7.anchor: حيث لم يف بها ولم يراع حقها

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:70-72/r8.claim: An alternative takes the trust as obedience, natural or voluntary; its offer is a request to the willing and divine willing of acts from others, while carrying can mean betrayal or failure.
